**Filters by Feature**
----------------------

Each feature in the platform supports different types of filters, allowing you to answer targeted questions about user behavior and performance.

### Web Analytics

Filters in Web Analytics help you break down traffic and session data to see how different sources, campaigns, and user types impact site performance.

*   **Session Filters:** Ads Platform, Traffic Source, Session Tag, Viewed Page, Returning Users, New Users
    

*   **Custom Filters**

Filters in Funnels reveal how specific user groups move through your conversion paths. You can see where different audiences drop off and how experiments impact performance.

*   **Ecommerce Filters:** Average Order Value, A/B Tests

### Heatmaps

Filters in Heatmaps let you visually compare how different user groups interact with your pages. This makes it easy to spot behavior differences and optimize layouts for each audience.

* * *

**How to Use Filters**
----------------------

You can apply filters across Analytics, Funnels, Heatmaps, and Recordings directly from the main header navigation bar.

To apply filters:

1.  Open the feature you want to analyze (ie: Heatmaps).
    
2.  Click the **Filters** dropdown.
    
3.  Choose from the available pre-built filters under **Session** or **Ecommerce** columns.
    
4.  To create a new cohort, scroll to **Custom Filters** and select **Add Custom Filter**. Your saved custom filters will be available for reuse later.
    
5.  After choosing your desired filters, click **Apply** to view the filtered data.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652107781/33ad48594620b6e198ed8370f0dd/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=30551a9ed80a01df54a7eb445554d352819ad668e1913f288f88ecb0f543f667&req=dSYiFMh%2BmoZXWPMW1HO4zeNjJFTfEfDDYm0OPTJwbPHAd57RFaCIvlaKpvJ2%0ASpKy9KOudfzDnGN86ns%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652107781/33ad48594620b6e198ed8370f0dd/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=30551a9ed80a01df54a7eb445554d352819ad668e1913f288f88ecb0f543f667&req=dSYiFMh%2BmoZXWPMW1HO4zeNjJFTfEfDDYm0OPTJwbPHAd57RFaCIvlaKpvJ2%0ASpKy9KOudfzDnGN86ns%3D%0A)

  
​

* * *

​

**Comparing User Segments in Heatmaps**
---------------------------------------

Heatmaps allow you to directly compare two user segments to see how behavior differs on the same page elements.

1.  Click the **Filters** dropdown.
    
2.  Select your first filter segment.
    
3.  Click the **Compare** button in the Filters dropdown.
    
4.  Select a second segment within the side panel to compare against the first.
    
    [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1696235231/9d40b69a6f856954d9cf501deb21/AD_4nXc0NO9quKscJcrefSLd1YksL_ZA3FMxsVVEsDJyptIwI3y0mFBYrVWJ9uhfoVCn7iu3KviuQ0oqlQKJhiBnFlVYwAVRcLvVP1Khq7nFrKqbnzBvVmwCaRXqNwLmZ-69fZEm96_O?expires=1789486200&signature=5ca93b08e05dcd692e06774f6e1aeb8b1f21378b50eb32b1c459a3ffb9f6a2af&req=dSYuEMt9mINcWPMW1HO4zb8zeoep5ESH0h1wPikYWe5fnDOhQGE%2BC5SVsfDe%0AR5H9%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1696235231/9d40b69a6f856954d9cf501deb21/AD_4nXc0NO9quKscJcrefSLd1YksL_ZA3FMxsVVEsDJyptIwI3y0mFBYrVWJ9uhfoVCn7iu3KviuQ0oqlQKJhiBnFlVYwAVRcLvVP1Khq7nFrKqbnzBvVmwCaRXqNwLmZ-69fZEm96_O?expires=1789486200&signature=5ca93b08e05dcd692e06774f6e1aeb8b1f21378b50eb32b1c459a3ffb9f6a2af&req=dSYuEMt9mINcWPMW1HO4zb8zeoep5ESH0h1wPikYWe5fnDOhQGE%2BC5SVsfDe%0AR5H9%0A)
    
5.  Click **Apply Filters** to see the filtered data.
    
6.  To review the compared data, select specific elements to see data of both user segments.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1696234634/e7e4a750f008c466b11e023d790c/AD_4nXdu-QW5C4apS1Wc89oi1S75BUkJUNziwXxUY52TAf7mQKcjb6z4HkGs6R0iJrHyQEYm4uYFzTYOM7UslXxQWVdUbAuQWjrdhCqZ_fJ_xRy_ryZFUnmBLM9xolyuWgq8XWeZ89RbZQ?expires=1789486200&signature=19938787bc493d275f649373c956848bc4acc0c5d5fd26dc4e5d23f05974412b&req=dSYuEMt9mYdcXfMW1HO4zSt2%2F6S2Z%2BCcb1WHb6xUNf%2BROVIlDEp1cLTsJ0Bj%0Aapdu%2Bs0FKRPghmaa3Ss%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1696234634/e7e4a750f008c466b11e023d790c/AD_4nXdu-QW5C4apS1Wc89oi1S75BUkJUNziwXxUY52TAf7mQKcjb6z4HkGs6R0iJrHyQEYm4uYFzTYOM7UslXxQWVdUbAuQWjrdhCqZ_fJ_xRy_ryZFUnmBLM9xolyuWgq8XWeZ89RbZQ?expires=1789486200&signature=19938787bc493d275f649373c956848bc4acc0c5d5fd26dc4e5d23f05974412b&req=dSYuEMt9mYdcXfMW1HO4zSt2%2F6S2Z%2BCcb1WHb6xUNf%2BROVIlDEp1cLTsJ0Bj%0Aapdu%2Bs0FKRPghmaa3Ss%3D%0A)

This helps you understand how different types of users interact with your site, for example, comparing new vs. returning users to spot differences in engagement or conversion.

* * *

**When to Use Filters: Scenarios for Smarter Analysis**
-------------------------------------------------------

Filters are especially helpful when you want to zoom in on specific user behaviors or campaigns. Some common use cases include:

*   Analyzing traffic from a particular ad or email campaign.
    
*   Identifying patterns among returning visitors who engage more deeply.
    
*   Spotting usability issues by reviewing sessions with high rage clicks.
    
*   Understanding how purchasers vs. non-purchasers interact differently.

Google Tag Manager (GTM) Installation Guide
===========================================

Installing Heatmap.com Using Google Tag Manager

Updated this week

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508574-google-tag-manager-gtm-installation-guide#h_30c243cd94)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508574-google-tag-manager-gtm-installation-guide#h_fc7c1c1a8d)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508574-google-tag-manager-gtm-installation-guide#h_1c13441676)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508574-google-tag-manager-gtm-installation-guide#h_5c576c8929)

While we recommend adding the heatmap code snippets directly to your website, some website owners prefer tag managers such as Google Tag Manager (GTM). This guide will walk you through the process of installing Heatmap.com using GTM.

**Accessing your Heatmap Tracking Code Snippet & Heatmap Conversion Code Snippets:**
====================================================================================

In order to access your **code snippets,** you can follow these steps:

1.  Go to the Settings tab within your portal.
    
2.  Click "Snippet"
    
3.  Here you will see two codes available to copy:
    
    *   The Heatmap Tracking Code Snippet for tracking sessions
        
    *   The Heatmap Conversion Code Snippet for tracking revenue
        
    

For purposes of this guide, we will use Shopify snippets as an installation example.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652087261/234e74d62ec837fd8bee6e97fa9d/image+%2817%29.png?expires=1789486200&signature=6deff1362d0f536742d167aa3ebabb97b6ce0e936aace4ab4b7601f004faae14&req=dSYiFMl2moNZWPMW1HO4zWD05uyT4An1HIeDsA3AvxMFA413atrgekODzHvj%0AWhQTVcpEZU70pskfRDM%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652087261/234e74d62ec837fd8bee6e97fa9d/image+%2817%29.png?expires=1789486200&signature=6deff1362d0f536742d167aa3ebabb97b6ce0e936aace4ab4b7601f004faae14&req=dSYiFMl2moNZWPMW1HO4zWD05uyT4An1HIeDsA3AvxMFA413atrgekODzHvj%0AWhQTVcpEZU70pskfRDM%3D%0A)

* * *

Installing your Heatmap Tracking Code Snippet & Heatmap Conversion Code Snippets
================================================================================

**Installing the _theme.liquid_ Heatmap Tracking Code Snippet**
---------------------------------------------------------------

**1\. Access Google Tag Manager**

*   Log in to your Google Tag Manager account
    
*   Select the container for the website where you want to install Heatmap.com
    

**2\. Create a New Tag**

*   Click on "Tags" in the left sidebar
    
*   Click the "New" button to create a new tag

**Installing the Heatmap Conversion Code Snippet Pixel**
--------------------------------------------------------

We want to inject the **Heatmap Conversion Code Snippets** **(not the _theme.liquid_ Heatmap Tracking Code Snippet)** only when an event is triggered. Below are the steps to have this done in GTM

**Step 1: Get Your Site ID**

*   Log in to your **Heatmap dashboard**.
    
*   Go to **Settings → Snippet**.
    
*   Scroll down to the **Conversion Code Snippet** section.
    
*   In the auto-generated code, look for the number passed into
    
    initializePixel(XXXX), which will give you your Site ID.
    
    *   Example: initializePixel(4309) → your Site ID is 4309.
        
    
*   Copy this number, you’ll need it for the snippet below.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1681653501/ef2e119d9f64bc728e8beca06ae1/AD_4nXdud2vi7ZwA_p4of4l257bXD1QAroJrg-dvRBvUYmTny7jYUsLo6jPfkMWfEScm7TMUqciDgV8zKeN5GqxFJsfWXQLhK-sdGUCeYPW6cP0ZBxbfeNQ3I7q7VGqt7n63pl1lxrZe?expires=1789486200&signature=a29965f9c9a11440fef2abec932510066d853ef65ff55b7acf59ec9fd7eb5827&req=dSYvF897noRfWPMW1HO4zU1r1xDfTPif8B%2BKS9nUw%2BxNBAVqGPxF%2FdIpARY1%0AH2L2YpUsIiw1CXupWpI%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1681653501/ef2e119d9f64bc728e8beca06ae1/AD_4nXdud2vi7ZwA_p4of4l257bXD1QAroJrg-dvRBvUYmTny7jYUsLo6jPfkMWfEScm7TMUqciDgV8zKeN5GqxFJsfWXQLhK-sdGUCeYPW6cP0ZBxbfeNQ3I7q7VGqt7n63pl1lxrZe?expires=1789486200&signature=a29965f9c9a11440fef2abec932510066d853ef65ff55b7acf59ec9fd7eb5827&req=dSYvF897noRfWPMW1HO4zU1r1xDfTPif8B%2BKS9nUw%2BxNBAVqGPxF%2FdIpARY1%0AH2L2YpUsIiw1CXupWpI%3D%0A)

**Step 2: Set Up a Custom Trigger**

*   Go to “**Triggers**” in GTM and click on “**New**”
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1365045796/c4c1843d964572ab0d507162b6cf/AD_4nXeamdfNOJHQFLNW_pjevF6Opg_rICfCMd9DteD3Axd1DBKlk1q5ZoIDwZebWrcZ71Ro1_P3-whQSEO-C1H0MIAg7nasUMwyMGhYKa97jrU25BrPnf2K-e36QB0H26RN0PPkTQm2o6LkJmz3leaKkBMBkXPt?expires=1789486200&signature=d43cb6c8061d1b15e91e060a53f02acf6677fa1049b5f96702d5febf0745d187&req=dSMhE8l6mIZWX%2FMW1HO4zTCryJts18KIm4qM0uLsnqAIC0fU3Pv79C3Fb3je%0AzmNHpmJf5p5hcxEu2Vk%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1365045796/c4c1843d964572ab0d507162b6cf/AD_4nXeamdfNOJHQFLNW_pjevF6Opg_rICfCMd9DteD3Axd1DBKlk1q5ZoIDwZebWrcZ71Ro1_P3-whQSEO-C1H0MIAg7nasUMwyMGhYKa97jrU25BrPnf2K-e36QB0H26RN0PPkTQm2o6LkJmz3leaKkBMBkXPt?expires=1789486200&signature=d43cb6c8061d1b15e91e060a53f02acf6677fa1049b5f96702d5febf0745d187&req=dSMhE8l6mIZWX%2FMW1HO4zTCryJts18KIm4qM0uLsnqAIC0fU3Pv79C3Fb3je%0AzmNHpmJf5p5hcxEu2Vk%3D%0A)

*   Select “**Custom Event”** as the trigger type.
    
*   Name the event as “**Purchases**” or “**orderCompleted**” to match your platform's purchase event.
    
*   Set the condition so that the event is triggered only when the event name equals Purchase.

*   Save the trigger with the name “**Purchase Trigger**.”

**Step 3: Create a Custom Tag**

*   Go to “**Tags”** in GTM and create a “**New Tag**.”
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1365045807/aa2aada8afdad7f24ccaa3683a36/AD_4nXcSdHVZrOsrCq8c8cJiXFnDGuEJ7HDLRDDAthHSMslaBtzVwmLfJ0Vd7kKR3gz3i-IjZyg-6nBMpgjcGPfdDekujIEC23A0na87qBo7-X0CmXxY3Rt7uYefftuJ4ikydsa4l75SztUVYbVWsmKuhmLwfGGw?expires=1789486200&signature=95cbf1de3ded952545313d562e612d30c494ba8436d1aa0d636ab016b9c53770&req=dSMhE8l6mIlfXvMW1HO4zdLeflkDaInIGMvFoCwh6H69snZ1CJjeRytmFA8s%0A3HAZt9GE3mNM4%2FtW7iI%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1365045807/aa2aada8afdad7f24ccaa3683a36/AD_4nXcSdHVZrOsrCq8c8cJiXFnDGuEJ7HDLRDDAthHSMslaBtzVwmLfJ0Vd7kKR3gz3i-IjZyg-6nBMpgjcGPfdDekujIEC23A0na87qBo7-X0CmXxY3Rt7uYefftuJ4ikydsa4l75SztUVYbVWsmKuhmLwfGGw?expires=1789486200&signature=95cbf1de3ded952545313d562e612d30c494ba8436d1aa0d636ab016b9c53770&req=dSMhE8l6mIlfXvMW1HO4zdLeflkDaInIGMvFoCwh6H69snZ1CJjeRytmFA8s%0A3HAZt9GE3mNM4%2FtW7iI%3D%0A)

*   Name this tag something descriptive, like “**Heatmap Conversion Code Snippet**”.
    
*   Under **Tag Configuration**, select **Custom HTML** and paste the code below, replacing \[YOUR HEATMAP SITE ID\] with your Site ID from Step 1.
    

<script>  
function heatmapLoadConversionSnippet(url) {  
 var script = document.createElement('script');  
 script.type = 'text/javascript';  
 script.src = url;  
 script.async = false;  
 script.defer = true;  
 document.head.appendChild(script);  
}  
heatmapLoadConversionSnippet("https://dashboard.heatmap.com/conversions.js?siteId=\[REPLACE WITH YOUR HEATMAP SITE ID\]&dataLayer=populate");  
</script>

**Step 4: Publish the GTM Container**

*   Review your setup and go to “**Submit**” in GTM to publish the changes.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1365045803/a1ff5dbe8696c94c2c4bf76a0ea2/AD_4nXdfwTN7lauEoocXOXzu_rebqn7-4MG6y667tlBcdB8hTvapPqVJ8J09bsGmWIHF7_Wgq8rOMmyUEdKFyxR0KUJ7PjfHNsLFrn74wfK5dSUqyQFG6pmDeSeE-xMq1ihnQEUbxUwUg6AceO3GM-JXg-Xxh-Q?expires=1789486200&signature=dc606fe2955554c408907458908e541cd8417944241cd744d60c1445c64e7531&req=dSMhE8l6mIlfWvMW1HO4zfrjvCAZZ5OAZ3arsUEKiAA4dsMyJnmRD1IPfH0k%0AbO13S2CZ4uZ3aQqvoq8%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1365045803/a1ff5dbe8696c94c2c4bf76a0ea2/AD_4nXdfwTN7lauEoocXOXzu_rebqn7-4MG6y667tlBcdB8hTvapPqVJ8J09bsGmWIHF7_Wgq8rOMmyUEdKFyxR0KUJ7PjfHNsLFrn74wfK5dSUqyQFG6pmDeSeE-xMq1ihnQEUbxUwUg6AceO3GM-JXg-Xxh-Q?expires=1789486200&signature=dc606fe2955554c408907458908e541cd8417944241cd744d60c1445c64e7531&req=dSMhE8l6mIlfWvMW1HO4zfrjvCAZZ5OAZ3arsUEKiAA4dsMyJnmRD1IPfH0k%0AbO13S2CZ4uZ3aQqvoq8%3D%0A)

*   Click “**Publish**.”

* * *

**Snippet Installation Verification**
-------------------------------------

To ensure your snippets were correctly installed via GTM, we recommend the following steps:

1.  Visit your website, interact with it as a user would, and complete a test purchase.
    
2.  Open "GTM Preview Mode" to confirm that the Purchase Trigger correctly fires the custom tag after a purchase.
    
3.  Verify your snippet in the Heatmap Portal after confirmation in GTM. You should be able to see data populate after about 12 hours of data. To verify your snippet:
    
    *   Log in to your Heatmap.com account and go to the Settings tab within your portal.
        
    *   Click "Snippet"
        
    *   Click the "Verify My Snippet" button in the bottom right corner.
        
        [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1633438217/487f5d72dccb4f988df744f1bb90/Screenshot-2B2025-07-22-2Bat-2B5_06_21-E2-80-AFPM-2B1.png?expires=1789486200&signature=b2bef6d9bdd1ce266fdc2d027628f809849e4bc72dbfcf4ad72bca98bbcc6543&req=dSYkFc19lYNeXvMW1HO4zWmiBKUcIuhQGewbTC%2BtCZfbCJ7kO9Xf3nvwLT4b%0Ap0T9%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1633438217/487f5d72dccb4f988df744f1bb90/Screenshot-2B2025-07-22-2Bat-2B5_06_21-E2-80-AFPM-2B1.png?expires=1789486200&signature=b2bef6d9bdd1ce266fdc2d027628f809849e4bc72dbfcf4ad72bca98bbcc6543&req=dSYkFc19lYNeXvMW1HO4zWmiBKUcIuhQGewbTC%2BtCZfbCJ7kO9Xf3nvwLT4b%0Ap0T9%0A)
        
    *   You'll receive a pop-up validating if the snippet was installed correctly. If you don't see any data after 24 hours or believe there is a data collection issue, double-check that both snippets are correctly installed.
        
    

* * *

**Troubleshooting**
-------------------

### Common issues:

*   Data not appearing: Ensure your GTM container is properly installed on your website
    
*   Partial data: Check if your trigger is correctly set to fire on all desired pages
    

### **Best Practices**

*   Use Google Tag Manager's preview mode to test your tag before publishing
    
*   If you have multiple domains, create separate tags for each in GTM
    
*   Regularly check your GTM setup to ensure all tags are firing correctly
    

* * *

**Need Help?**
--------------

If you have questions or run into any issues while using Heatmap, our support team is here to help. Contact us anytime at [Support@heatmap.com](mailto:Support@heatmap.com)
.

**Troubleshooting Guide: Traffic to My Landing Page is Not Tracked Correctly**

If traffic to your landing page is not being tracked properly, follow this step-by-step guide to troubleshoot and resolve the issue.

1\. Are You Using a 3rd Party Page Builder?
-------------------------------------------

**Common Issue**: If you're using a 3rd party page builder like Replo, Zipify, or GemPages, additional setup is required to track custom-built pages that fall outside Shopify’s standard theme structure.

**Steps for 3rd Party Page Builders:**
--------------------------------------

1.  **Install the Heatmap.com Tracking Code in Your Shopify Theme**  
    Make sure the main Heatmap.com tracking code is installed in your Shopify theme as usual.
    
2.  **Identify Your Page Builder**  
    If you're using Replo, Zipify, or GemPages, follow the specific instructions below.
    

* * *

2\. Specific Instructions for Popular Page Builders:
----------------------------------------------------

**Replo**
---------

1.  Log in to your Replo dashboard.
    
2.  Navigate to **Settings > Integrations**.
    
3.  In the **Custom Code** or **Header Scripts** section, paste your Heatmap.com tracking code.
    
4.  Save your changes.
    

**Zipify Pages**
----------------

1.  In your Shopify admin, go to **Apps > Zipify Pages**.
    
2.  Navigate to **Settings > Tracking**.
    
3.  In the **Header Code** section, add your Heatmap.com tracking code.
    
4.  Click **Save** to apply.
    

**GemPages**
------------

1.  Open the GemPages editor.
    
2.  Click on **Settings** in the left sidebar.
    
3.  Go to the **Custom Code** tab.
    
4.  Paste your Heatmap.com tracking code in the **Header** section.
    
5.  Click **Save** to apply changes.
    

* * *

3\. Verifying Installation
--------------------------

After installing the tracking code:

1.  **Publish or Update** a page created with your page builder.
    
2.  Use Heatmap.com's **verification tool** to confirm tracking is working.
    
3.  Perform a **test interaction** on the page and check if it appears in your Heatmap.com dashboard.
    

* * *

4\. Troubleshooting Steps
-------------------------

If tracking still isn’t working:

*   **Check Installation**: Ensure you've installed the code in both your Shopify theme and the page builder settings.
    
*   **Clear Cache**: If your page builder has a caching system, clear the cache to ensure changes take effect.
    
*   **Verify Tracking Code**: Make sure you are using the correct tracking code for your Heatmap.com account.
    

* * *

5\. General Installation Instructions
-------------------------------------

If you’re **not using a 3rd party page builder**, follow these steps:

1.  Confirm the **Heatmap.com tracking code** is installed in your Shopify theme in the `<head>` section of your HTML.
    
2.  Make sure there are no typos or accidental modifications in the tracking code.
    
3.  Clear your **Shopify theme cache** and verify the code is running properly.
    

* * *

6\. Need Further Assistance?
----------------------------

If these steps don’t resolve the issue, contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
. Provide:

*   Your Shopify store URL
    
*   Details about your page builder setup
    
*   Any steps you've already taken for troubleshooting
    

* * *

Last Updated: 10/21/2024
------------------------

Ensure you follow proper installation steps across all page-building tools to get the most accurate data from Heatmap.com.

# Screen Recordings | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517088-screen-recordings#main-content)

Screen Recordings
=================

Screen Recordings

Updated this week

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517088-screen-recordings#h_71aa74705a)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517088-screen-recordings#h_f857f0c1c5)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517088-screen-recordings#h_c2b83bf52d)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517088-screen-recordings#h_7c1b51a4e8)

Screen Recordings capture sequential videos of user interactions on your website. They provide a detailed view of how users navigate, engage, and interact with various elements, revealing real-time behavioral patterns.  
​  
Unlike heatmaps, which show single screens, screen recordings offer an end-to-end, chronological view of user sessions you can watch.

  
The biggest differentiator between Heatmap.com and similar software is that our platform _ties revenue to screen recordings_, just like the heatmaps do.  
​  
You can filter for Average Order Value and high-value customers, users who did not purchase, and a range of infinite filters such as traffic sources, browser types, device types, and geographic locations.

  
You can share recordings across marketing and engineering teams. All of our screen recordings automatically exclude sensitive user data to maintain compliance with privacy standards (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).  
​

* * *

  
**Use Screen Recordings to Optimize User Experiences**
---------------------------------------------------------

Screen Recordings are invaluable for understanding user behavior, identifying issues, and refining your site’s performance. Some common use cases include:

*   **Pinpointing Friction Points**: Identify where users struggle, abandon tasks, or experience confusion.  
    ​
    
*   **Analyzing Conversion Journeys**: Understand user actions that lead to conversions or detect drop-offs.  
    ​
    
*   **Testing New Features**: Monitor user interaction with new elements, such as a bundle builder or redesigned landing pages.  
    ​
    
*   **Segment-Specific Insights**: Compare behaviors across user segments, such as mobile vs. desktop visitors.  
    ​
    

* * *

  
  
**How to Access and Use Screen Recordings**
-------------------------------------------------

_Recording above showing how to access and use screen recordings on the Heatmap platform_

1.  **Access the Recordings**: Navigate to the left-hand menu in your dashboard and click **“Screen Recordings.”**  
    ​
    
2.  **Filter Recordings**: Use filters to focus on specific sessions by _duration, device type, Purchases,_ or any user segment you want to analyze**.**  
    ​
    
3.  **Analyze Patterns**:
    
    *   Identify common navigation paths, frequent interactions, or recurring issues.
        
    *   Compare sessions to identify differences in behavior, such as why mobile users might have lower conversion rates.  
        ​
        
    
4.  **Share Insights**: Share recordings with teammates to collaborate on resolving issues or enhancing designs.
    

* * *

**When to Use Screen Recordings? Key Scenarios**
------------------------------------------------

*   **During A/B Testing**: Observe how users interact with different versions of a feature or layout to identify the better-performing option.  
    ​
    
*   **Monitoring New Launches**: Track engagement with newly added pages, forms, or promotional content.  
    ​
    
*   **Troubleshooting Performance Drops**: Investigate sessions tied to low-conversion segments, such as mobile users, to pinpoint specific blockers.  
    ​
    
*   **Post-Implementation Reviews**: Assess user feedback and behavior after deploying a feature to refine further improvements.  
    ​
    

* * *

**Need Help?**
--------------

If you have questions or run into any issues while using Heatmap, our support team is here to help. Contact us anytime at [Support@heatmap.com](mailto:Support@heatmap.com)
.

# Change Website Version View | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/11836689-change-website-version-view#main-content)

Change Website Version View
===========================

How to View Previous Theme Updates, Previous Screenshots, and Ended A/B Test Data in Heatmap

August 12, 2025

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/11836689-change-website-version-view#h_1751e60824)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/11836689-change-website-version-view#h_198d8f8027)

The Web Versioning Feature lets you view how your website looked and performed at any point in the past, especially useful when reviewing ended A/B tests or checking for older theme updates.

This feature pulls up historical screenshots and user interaction data from specific time periods. It’s not limited to A/B tests and can also help you:

*   **See previous theme versions** active during specific timeframes
    
*   **Access screenshots** that may no longer appear in the current view
    
*   **Review layout or content changes** from older versions of the page
    
*   **Analyse user behavior** from older A/B test variants
    

**How to View Previous Website Versions**
=========================================

If you'd like a video walkthrough of the View Previous Version feature, watch this video below:

1.  Go to the **Heatmap** feature and find the specific page you'd like to review.
    
2.  Use the **Date Picker** at the top of the screen to choose the time range you want to review and click **View Previous Versions**.
    
3.  Select the appropriate display you'd like to analyze and click **Load Selected Version** to populate the data.
    
4.  Heatmap will re-load the page with the appropriate display and provide visual data (clicks, scroll depth, etc.) for that version of the page.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1635840245/0948c4923c4b8889a97480e09d57/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=cccee4203319970d1741988be546ca2fe5c09febe9766e320d24971bfa8f1f2f&req=dSYkE8F6nYNbXPMW1HO4zY5SqkBhbF8gF08TK6KRRzFV%2BgaGBFf7qx%2BoR9bb%0AC8obplVvyeMn%2B9oawHg%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1635840245/0948c4923c4b8889a97480e09d57/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=cccee4203319970d1741988be546ca2fe5c09febe9766e320d24971bfa8f1f2f&req=dSYkE8F6nYNbXPMW1HO4zY5SqkBhbF8gF08TK6KRRzFV%2BgaGBFf7qx%2BoR9bb%0AC8obplVvyeMn%2B9oawHg%3D%0A)

⚠️ If a screenshot seems missing or outdated, it’s often because the layout has changed. Use the Web Versioning Feature to view the correct version by adjusting the date range.

* * *

View Ended A/B Test Variants
============================

If you're trying to view data from previous A/B tests that have already ended on Heatmap, you'll need to change the website view. Following the steps above, you should be able to find the specific variants from your test in the designated date ranges of the experiment.

Please reach out to [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 with any questions.

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060195-how-can-i-set-up-heatmap-ad-integrations#h_29f564dce0)

**Overview**
------------

**What is Heatmap Ad Integration?**
-----------------------------------

The Heatmap Ad Integration feature allows you to track and analyze user behavior from specific advertising campaigns. It connects your ad platforms (Facebook, Google, TikTok, X/Twitter) with your heatmap data, enabling you to see exactly how visitors from each ad campaign interact with your website.  
​

**Which ad platforms are supported?**
-------------------------------------

Currently supported platforms include:

*   Facebook (including Facebook Ads)
    
*   Google (Google Ads)
    
*   TikTok (TikTok Ads)
    
*   X/Twitter (Twitter Ads)
    
*   Klaviyo
    

**How does it work?**
---------------------

When users click on your ads, they're directed to your website with UTM parameters that identify the ad source. Our system tracks all their interactions (clicks, scrolls, page navigation) and allows you to filter this data by specific ad campaigns.

  
**Getting Started**
----------------------

**How do I connect my ad platforms?**
-------------------------------------

There are two ways to connect your ad platforms:  
​

**Method 1: Through Settings**

1.  Navigate to Settings > Integrations
    
2.  Click "Connect" next to your desired platform
    
3.  A pop-up will appear for account authorization
    
4.  Select your account and click "Continue"
    
5.  The platform will show as "Connected"
    

**Method 2: Through Heatmap Filters**

1.  Go to your Heatmap dashboard
    
2.  Click on "Filters"
    
3.  Select "AD Platform" filter
    
4.  Click "Connect" for your desired platform
    
5.  Complete the authorization process
    

**Do I need special permissions for my ad accounts?**
-----------------------------------------------------

Yes, you'll need admin or appropriate permissions on your ad accounts to authorize the connection. Each platform has its own requirements:

*   Facebook: Admin access to ad accounts
    
*   Google: Manager access to Google Ads
    
*   TikTok: Advertiser account access
    
*   X/Twitter: Premium verification may be required for ads
    

**What happens after I connect a platform?**
--------------------------------------------

Once connected, the system will:

*   Fetch all your ad accounts for that platform
    
*   Display available campaigns
    
*   Begin tracking sessions from those campaigns
    
*   Enable filtering options in your heatmap dashboard
    

**Using the Feature**
---------------------

**How do I view heatmap data for specific ad campaigns?**
---------------------------------------------------------

1.  Go to your Heatmap dashboard
    
2.  Click the "Filters" button
    
3.  Select "Ads Platform" from the filter options
    
4.  Choose your connected platform
    
5.  Select specific campaigns you want to analyze
    
6.  The heatmap will update to show only sessions from those campaigns
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2283943568/f6ebda37b9940df7ab6e38a265c3/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=6c842d58d1c2e0e836d413f19253a6dcc64ca38c76d0d1d5b7f94f2ecba8edb3&req=diIvFcB6noRZUfMW1HO4zS%2F9GcpCuqRm7xjucIf22FbAbknrsbKT2GdBgJ1g%0AJnRgk2JnSTFnkdRhGB0%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2283943568/f6ebda37b9940df7ab6e38a265c3/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=6c842d58d1c2e0e836d413f19253a6dcc64ca38c76d0d1d5b7f94f2ecba8edb3&req=diIvFcB6noRZUfMW1HO4zS%2F9GcpCuqRm7xjucIf22FbAbknrsbKT2GdBgJ1g%0AJnRgk2JnSTFnkdRhGB0%3D%0A)

**Can I filter by multiple campaigns?**
---------------------------------------

Yes, you can select multiple campaigns from the same platform or even across different platforms to compare performance.  
​

**What metrics can I see?**
---------------------------

The integration provides:

*   Number of sessions per campaign
    
*   Device breakdown (desktop/mobile/tablet)
    
*   User interactions (clicks, scrolls, time on page)
    
*   Navigation paths through your site
    
*   Conversion tracking (if configured)
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2283945615/b7aef0d81694c2fdbdad85fac6c7/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=c96cd057502d95498835eda02fa90ff0fe02d708fc0eb8bb045d5210668ecb40&req=diIvFcB6mIdeXPMW1HO4zddzSqursY%2BMIleiwBJUgN1C%2FMIelXrYF61Wp4rV%0AC8NVog6Dsaqz5SnJxGg%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2283945615/b7aef0d81694c2fdbdad85fac6c7/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=c96cd057502d95498835eda02fa90ff0fe02d708fc0eb8bb045d5210668ecb40&req=diIvFcB6mIdeXPMW1HO4zddzSqursY%2BMIleiwBJUgN1C%2FMIelXrYF61Wp4rV%0AC8NVog6Dsaqz5SnJxGg%3D%0A)

**How do I disconnect a platform?**
-----------------------------------

1.  Go to Settings > Integrations
    
2.  Find the connected platform
    
3.  Click the "Disconnect" button
    
4.  Confirm the disconnection
    

Note: Disconnecting will not delete historical data but will stop tracking new sessions from that platform.  
​

**Tracking and Analytics**
--------------------------

**How are sessions tracked from ads?**
--------------------------------------

Sessions are tracked using UTM parameters automatically added to your ad URLs. These parameters include:

*   utm\_source (platform name)
    
*   utm\_medium (ad type)
    
*   utm\_campaign (campaign name)
    
*   utm\_content (ad creative identifier)
    
*   Platform-specific parameters (fbclid, gclid, ttclid)
    
*   ad\_id ( the ad identifier )
    
*   adset\_id ( the adset or adgroup identifier )
    
*   campaign\_id ( the campaign Identifier )
    

**Why don't I see any data after connecting?**
----------------------------------------------

Several reasons might cause this:

1.  **No active campaigns**: Ensure you have running campaigns with traffic
    
2.  **Recent connection**: It may take up to 30 minutes for initial data to appear
    
3.  **UTM parameters**: Verify your ads include proper tracking parameters
    
4.  **Ad approval**: Some platforms require ad approval before they go live
    
5.  **Tracking script**: Ensure your heatmap tracking script is properly installed
    

**Can I see historical data from before I connected?**
------------------------------------------------------

No, the integration only tracks sessions from the moment you connect your ad platform. Historical ad performance data is not retroactively added.  
​

**How accurate is the tracking?**
---------------------------------

Tracking accuracy depends on:

*   Proper UTM parameter implementation
    
*   Users not using ad blockers
    
*   Correct heatmap script installation
    
*   Cookie acceptance by users
    

**Troubleshooting**
-------------------

**My platform shows as connected but I see no campaigns**
---------------------------------------------------------

This could happen if:

*   You have no active campaigns in that ad account
    
*   The account permissions are insufficient
    
*   There's a sync delay (wait 15-30 minutes)
    
*   Try disconnecting and reconnecting the platform
    

**Sessions aren't appearing in the filter**
-------------------------------------------

Check the following:

1.  Verify ads are actively running and receiving clicks
    
2.  Confirm UTM parameters are present in your ad URLs
    
3.  Check that the heatmap tracking script is on all pages
    
4.  Ensure cookies are enabled for tracking
    
5.  Wait at least 30 minutes after generating test traffic
    

**I'm getting an authentication error**
---------------------------------------

*   Your ad platform session may have expired
    
*   Platform permissions may have changed
    
*   Try disconnecting and reconnecting the platform
    
*   Ensure you're using the correct account credentials
    

**Filter shows zero sessions but I know there's traffic**
---------------------------------------------------------

*   Double-check campaign selection in the filter
    
*   Verify date range includes when ads were running
    
*   Confirm UTM parameters match expected values
    
*   Clear browser cache and refresh the dashboard
    

**Best Practices**
------------------

**Setting up campaigns for optimal tracking**
---------------------------------------------

1.  Always use consistent UTM naming conventions
    
2.  Test tracking with a small budget first
    
3.  Create separate campaigns for different objectives
    
4.  Use descriptive campaign names for easy filtering
    

**Analyzing the data**
----------------------

*   Compare heatmaps between campaigns to identify best performers
    
*   Look for patterns in user behavior by device type
    
*   Use session recordings alongside heatmaps for deeper insights
    
*   Export data regularly for historical analysis
    

**Privacy and compliance**
--------------------------

*   Ensure you have proper consent for tracking users
    
*   Include privacy policy updates mentioning ad tracking
    
*   Comply with platform-specific privacy requirements
    
*   Respect user opt-outs and do-not-track settings
    

**Limitations**
---------------

**What are the current limitations?**
-------------------------------------

*   Real-time data may have a 15-30 minute delay
    
*   Maximum of 10,000 sessions per filter view
    
*   Some ad platforms require premium accounts
    
*   Cross-domain tracking requires additional setup
    

**Platform-specific limitations**
---------------------------------

*   **X/Twitter**: Requires premium verification for ads
    
*   **Google**: Ads API requires separate approval process
    
*   **Facebook**: Limited to accounts you admin
    
*   **TikTok**: Business account required
    

**Getting Help**
----------------

**Where can I get additional support?**
---------------------------------------

If you need further assistance:

*   Contact our support team through the help center
    
*   Check our video tutorials for visual guides
    
*   Join our community forum for tips from other users
    
*   Schedule a demo with our success team for advanced features
    

**How do I report a bug or request a feature?**
-----------------------------------------------

*   Use the feedback button in the dashboard
    
*   Email our product team directly
    
*   Submit detailed reports including screenshots
    
*   Include steps to reproduce any issues
    

* * *

  
Questions? Reach out to [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 - we're here to help you succeed.

# Warning: Lazy Loading May Affect Heatmap Accuracy | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023118-warning-lazy-loading-may-affect-heatmap-accuracy#main-content)

Warning: Lazy Loading May Affect Heatmap Accuracy
=================================================

Lazy loading, heatmap accuracy, initial page load, user interactions, script placement, scroll depth, data collection, Heatmap.com, page performance

October 21, 2024

**What is Lazy Loading?**

**Lazy loading is a technique that delays the loading of non-critical resources at page load time. It can improve initial page load performance, but may impact heatmap data collection.**

**The Issue with Lazy Loading**

**When the Heatmap.com script is lazy loaded:**

1.  **Initial user interactions may be missed**
    
2.  **Early page events might not be captured**
    
3.  **Scroll depth measurements could be inaccurate**
    

**This can lead to incomplete or misleading heatmap data, especially for above-the-fold content.**

**Recommended Solution**

**For optimal heatmap accuracy, we strongly recommend:**

1.  **Load the Heatmap.com script as early as possible in your page's <head> section**
    
2.  **Avoid using lazy loading techniques of our script**
    

**Implementation Best Practice**

**Place our script immediately after the opening <head> tag:**

**<head>**

**<script>**

**// Heatmap.com script here**

**</script>**

**<!-- Other head elements -->**

**</head>**

**This ensures our script loads promptly, capturing all user interactions from the moment the page starts rendering.**

**Need Help?**

**If you're unsure about your implementation or have concerns about data accuracy, please contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
. We're here to help ensure you get the most accurate and comprehensive heatmap data possible.**

# How does Heatmap.com affect my sites page speed? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023190-how-does-heatmap-com-affect-my-sites-page-speed#main-content)

How does Heatmap.com affect my sites page speed?
================================================

Site speed, asynchronous loading, minimal impact, data collection, performance monitoring, PageSpeed Insights, GTmetrix, analytics tools, site performance

October 21, 2024

**Overview**

At Heatmap.com, we understand the critical importance of site speed for user experience and website performance. We've designed our tracking script to have minimal impact on your website's loading time. Here's what you need to know about how Heatmap.com affects your site speed.

**Minimal Impact by Design**

*   Lightweight Script: Our tracking script is highly optimized and lightweight, typically adding less than 100kb to your page load.
    
*   Asynchronous Loading: The Heatmap.com script loads asynchronously, meaning it doesn't block other elements of your page from loading.
    
*   Efficient Data Collection: We use efficient methods to collect user interaction data without causing noticeable delays.
    

**Comparative Performance**

In tests across thousands of websites, Heatmap.com consistently outperforms other heatmap and analytics tools in terms of site speed impact:

*   On average, Heatmap.com adds less than 100ms to page load times.
    
*   This is significantly less than many other popular analytics and heatmap tools, which can add 300ms or more
    

**Real-World Impact**

For most websites, the impact of Heatmap.com on site speed is negligible:

*   Users typically won't notice any difference in load times
    
*   The slight increase in load time is offset by the valuable insights gained from our analytics
    

**Monitoring Your Site's Performance**

We encourage you to monitor your site's performance before and after installing Heatmap.com:

1.  Use tools like Google PageSpeed Insights or GTmetrix to measure your site speed
    
2.  **Compare results from before and after installing Heatmap.com**
    
3.  If you notice any significant changes, please contact our support team for assistance
    

**Best Practices for Maintaining Site Speed**

While using Heatmap.com:

1\. Keep your Heatmap.com script up to date

2\. Only install the script on pages you want to track

3\. Use our built-in Site Speed metric in your dashboard to monitor performance over time

**Our Commitment to Performance**

We continuously work on optimizing our script to minimize its impact on your site:

\- Regular performance audits and improvements

\- Staying up-to-date with the latest web performance best practices

**What If I Notice a Slowdown?**

If you believe Heatmap.com is significantly impacting your site speed:

1\. Verify the issue using speed testing tools

2\. Check that the Heatmap.com script is properly installed

3\. Contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 for personalized assistance

**Conclusion**

Heatmap.com is designed to provide valuable insights with minimal impact on your site's performance. Our commitment to efficiency means you can gain deep analytics without sacrificing speed. If you have any concerns or questions about site speed, don't hesitate to reach out to our support team.

Remember, the slight impact on load time is often far outweighed by the insights and improvements you can make based on Heatmap.com's data, potentially leading to overall better site performance and user experience.

# Troubleshooting: No Dots on Heatmap | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10022328-troubleshooting-no-dots-on-heatmap#main-content)

Troubleshooting: No Dots on Heatmap
===================================

Heatmap.com, no dots, header snippet, snippet installation, tracking issues, website cache, conflicting plugins, browser console, site ID, troubleshooting, support

October 21, 2024

**Troubleshooting: No Dots on Heatmap - Header Snippet Not Active**

If you're seeing no dots at all on your heatmap, it likely indicates that the Heatmap.com header snippet is not active on your website. This article will guide you through the troubleshooting process.

**Understanding the Issue**

When the header snippet is correctly installed and active, you should see dots on your heatmap representing user interactions. If no dots appear, it means no data is being collected, suggesting the snippet isn't functioning properly.

**Common Causes**

1\. Snippet not installed correctly

2\. Snippet blocked by security settings

3\. Caching issues

4\. Conflicts with other scripts

**Troubleshooting Steps**

1\. Verify Snippet Installation

\- Log into your website's backend or content management system.

\- Check if the Heatmap.com snippet is present in the \`<head>\` section of your website's HTML.

\- Ensure the snippet is placed before the closing \`</head>\` tag.

**2\. Check for Typos**

\- Compare the installed snippet with the original provided by Heatmap.com.

\- Look for any accidental modifications or typos.

**3\. Clear Website Cache**

\- Clear your website's cache in your content management system.

\- If using a caching plugin, purge its cache as well.

**4\. Disable Conflicting Plugins**

\- Temporarily disable other analytics or script-blocking plugins.

\- Re-check your heatmap to see if dots appear.

**5\. Check Browser Console for Errors**

\- Open your website in Chrome or Firefox.

\- Right-click and select "Inspect" or press F12.

\- Go to the "Console" tab.

\- Look for any error messages related to Heatmap.com.

**6\. Verify Your Site ID**

\- Ensure the Site ID in your snippet matches the one in your Heatmap.com account.

**7\. Test in Incognito Mode**

\- Open your website in an incognito/private browsing window.

\- This bypasses local browser caches and extensions.

**Still Not Working?**

If you've tried these steps and still see no dots:

1\. Double-check that your account is active and not paused.

2\. Ensure you're looking at the correct date range in your Heatmap.com dashboard.

3\. Verify that your website has received traffic since installing the snippet.

**Contacting Support**

If the issue persists, please contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 with the following information:

\- Your website URL

\- Screenshots of your header code where the snippet is installed

\- Any error messages from the browser console

\- Steps you've already taken to troubleshoot

Our team will be happy to assist you in getting your heatmap up and running.

Remember, accurate tracking is crucial for gaining valuable insights from Heatmap.com. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need any help!

Last Updated: 10/21/2024

# Google Tag Manager Integration with Heatmap.com | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023180-google-tag-manager-integration-with-heatmap-com#main-content)

Google Tag Manager Integration with Heatmap.com
===============================================

Google Tag Manager, tracking code, tag configuration, trigger setup, custom HTML, GTM container, all pages, data verification

October 21, 2024

Google Tag Manager (GTM) offers a convenient way to add Heatmap.com to your website without directly editing your site's code. This guide will walk you through the process of installing Heatmap.com using GTM.

**Prerequisites**

Before you begin, ensure you have:

1.  A Heatmap.com account
    
2.  Access to your Google Tag Manager account
    
3.  Your Heatmap.com tracking code
    

**Step-by-Step Installation Guide**

**1\. Access Google Tag Manager**

*   Log in to your Google Tag Manager account
    
*   Select the container for the website where you want to install Heatmap.com
    

**2\. Create a New Tag**

*   Click on "Tags" in the left sidebar
    
*   Click the "New" button to create a new tag
    

**3\. Configure the Tag**

*   Name your tag (e.g., "Heatmap.com Tracking")
    
*   Click on "Tag Configuration"
    
*   Choose "Custom HTML" as the tag type
    

**4\. Add Heatmap.com Tracking Code**

*   In the HTML field, paste your Heatmap.com tracking code
    

**5\. Set Trigger**

*   Click on "Triggering"
    
*   Select "All Pages" to have Heatmap.com track all pages on your site
    
*   If you want to limit tracking to specific pages, create a custom trigger
    

**6\. Save and Submit**

*   Click "Save" to save your new tag
    
*   Click "Submit" to push your changes live
    

**7\. Publish Your Changes**

*   Review your changes
    
*   Click "Publish" to make your tag live on your website
    

**Verifying Installation**

To ensure Heatmap.com is installed correctly:

*   Wait a few minutes after publishing your changes
    
*   Visit your website and perform some actions
    
*   Log in to your Heatmap.com dashboard
    
*   Check if data is being recorded
    

If you don't see data within 24 hours, please contact our support team.

**Troubleshooting**

Common issues include:

\- Data not appearing: Ensure your GTM container is properly installed on your website

\- Partial data: Check if your trigger is correctly set to fire on all desired pages

**Best Practices**

1.  Use Google Tag Manager's preview mode to test your tag before publishing
    
2.  If you have multiple domains, create separate tags for each in GTM
    
3.  Regularly check your GTM setup to ensure all tags are firing correctly
    

**Next Steps**

After successful installation:

1.  Set up goals and events in Heatmap.com
    
2.  Explore different heatmap types in your dashboard
    
3.  Consider setting up custom segments for more detailed analysis
    

Need further assistance? Contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

Remember, while GTM simplifies tag management, it's crucial to monitor your Heatmap.com data to ensure continuous and accurate tracking.

========================

Grouped heatmaps

Updated this week

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517113-introducing-groups-pages#h_3f83d3d94e)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517113-introducing-groups-pages#h_5c485888a2)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517113-introducing-groups-pages#h_bba4d11120)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517113-introducing-groups-pages#h_fdd33079f7)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517113-introducing-groups-pages#h_7368a3aa42)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517113-introducing-groups-pages#h_56ac16502e)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10517113-introducing-groups-pages#h_c61e5d897f)

The **Groups Pages** feature provides a unified view of heatmap analytics for pages that share similar templates and URL structures. This is particularly helpful for analyzing key metrics across related pages, such as product or collection pages.

**Please note:** you will see the highest-traffic page-type that you’re selecting, but the data is aggregated from all pages in the Group Type. All elements that appear on every page type in the Grouped Pages will have combined data and non-unique content will be discarded.

  
The following will show the best applications for this feature:

  
**Use Cases**
----------------

**Grouped Pages** streamline analytics for same-template pages. Some common use cases include:

*   **Product Page Templates**: Consolidate data for all product pages to uncover trends, such as effective CTAs or standout product images.  
    ​
    
*   **Navigation Analysis:** See how sessions flow through the site with a holistic view of user navigation.  
    ​
    
*   **Collection Page Templates**: Understand which collections generate the most engagement and optimize layouts to boost click-through rates.  
    ​
    
*   **Site-Wide Page Elements**: Analyze recurring elements like navigation bars, footers, or banners to consistently evaluate their performance.
    

* * *

**Accessing Grouped Pages**
---------------------------

To access Grouped Pages, navigate to the Filter button in any heatmap and navigate to the **Groups** section. Here, you'll find default groupings automatically created by Heatmap.com.

While default groups cannot be edited, you can easily [add new custom groups](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HFdRsbFTFPjASn6ZlttIy9B5rfcFWR15EfN_gZVweoc/edit#link)
 tailored to your needs.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481179585/b43ec4ce677d621840a018a66f9c/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=073b4415137349f40be5ebd78c466e75e4d2a26ce3da250e7be3ea484d54d4cf&req=diQvF8h5lIRXXPMW1HO4zelmarmkE8kd9%2BVw6RjtLJ8Bhw49WgQlgi8GDlb9%0AGBoN7d4Z80bDvGnVrxI%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481179585/b43ec4ce677d621840a018a66f9c/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=073b4415137349f40be5ebd78c466e75e4d2a26ce3da250e7be3ea484d54d4cf&req=diQvF8h5lIRXXPMW1HO4zelmarmkE8kd9%2BVw6RjtLJ8Bhw49WgQlgi8GDlb9%0AGBoN7d4Z80bDvGnVrxI%3D%0A)

* * *

**Understanding Grouped Pages Metrics**
---------------------------------------

**Grouped Page** analytics will contain a consolidation of metrics across all pages contained in the grouping. The heatmap view will be a screenshot of your highest traffic page within that group and the metrics will contain a sum of all the data across each page included within the grouping.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481193387/b7ca49aa9f357e1b96e9a9c56e26/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=0724a1dadf59c3d8ab873960f007517a11b9401c477863ddb372b1370ed28f06&req=diQvF8h3noJXXvMW1HO4zaZGbAsEa8JnQkiU7CYBKrk7MGrCFVYMCucS8H71%0AAT%2Fb0lOZXmAUxMgOARM%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481193387/b7ca49aa9f357e1b96e9a9c56e26/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=0724a1dadf59c3d8ab873960f007517a11b9401c477863ddb372b1370ed28f06&req=diQvF8h3noJXXvMW1HO4zaZGbAsEa8JnQkiU7CYBKrk7MGrCFVYMCucS8H71%0AAT%2Fb0lOZXmAUxMgOARM%3D%0A)

If you would like to see what pages are included in the group, you can click the ​​Edit icon (or the pencil-shaped icon next to the page group) and select URL list that pops up to the right.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481188907/861723c37b58ec9ed0d930464c72/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=00351a050236aebb104d00465f8b7f8e4a45b094fc806a2dee99d3a63a2597e6&req=diQvF8h2lYhfXvMW1HO4zRy0S3a3ZsKwhl68PmZR6KRySB8A4sStCJumUrAW%0AvNG7dXV%2B2PqdMIF3kFw%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481188907/861723c37b58ec9ed0d930464c72/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=00351a050236aebb104d00465f8b7f8e4a45b094fc806a2dee99d3a63a2597e6&req=diQvF8h2lYhfXvMW1HO4zRy0S3a3ZsKwhl68PmZR6KRySB8A4sStCJumUrAW%0AvNG7dXV%2B2PqdMIF3kFw%3D%0A)

You will now see a list of URLs that are included in the group

* * *

**Adding a New Group**
----------------------

Create custom groups to suit your specific business needs, such as grouping products that target a particular demographic.  
​

**To Create a New Group:**  
​

**Step 1: Click the Pages Menu** within a heatmap. Select the _Page Group tab_ and select **New Custom Group**.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481201380/170c000d731033751c62ca1f7331/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=cea2b54bee8502fd283456d5c052ef30070d562a187e14666a6ccd296fb3a5ed&req=diQvF8t%2BnIJXWfMW1HO4zZsM2304EvI0glZxt5zVoHBT0iXwAhRyJ0OP%2FRyR%0AOx26Awai8a20FtiBuxY%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481201380/170c000d731033751c62ca1f7331/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=cea2b54bee8502fd283456d5c052ef30070d562a187e14666a6ccd296fb3a5ed&req=diQvF8t%2BnIJXWfMW1HO4zZsM2304EvI0glZxt5zVoHBT0iXwAhRyJ0OP%2FRyR%0AOx26Awai8a20FtiBuxY%3D%0A)

**Step 2: Enter group details**, including a name and URL parameters.

**Step 3: Preview included URLs** by clicking the **Navigation arrow** button.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481207774/9545b909f1dc1dc3e1af94e950ea/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=37d818fd1e604a47dce0517a9706a398aabb5074d70f7fe7c94af50bb79e8a77&req=diQvF8t%2BmoZYXfMW1HO4zeT0InfQ3QFQpNIgwO7y2d20i%2F%2F50gySyDc%2F%2FbsL%0AQpYUZpqfxHFY7mvdW3o%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481207774/9545b909f1dc1dc3e1af94e950ea/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=37d818fd1e604a47dce0517a9706a398aabb5074d70f7fe7c94af50bb79e8a77&req=diQvF8t%2BmoZYXfMW1HO4zeT0InfQ3QFQpNIgwO7y2d20i%2F%2F50gySyDc%2F%2FbsL%0AQpYUZpqfxHFY7mvdW3o%3D%0A)

**Step 4:** Once everything looks good, click **Create New Group** to add the new group.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481211353/51420df8e5abe5b7a0b4e05781bc/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=400d83d40dae53a2c7fddf5895ad248f99ae9844468dae17b3e486c63258599a&req=diQvF8t%2FnIJaWvMW1HO4zflQ7Mala1bBDggfcRWq0%2FCtSLig9r6eCcfEa3Rj%0AUZrzV6bjTjDn0eKivCs%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2481211353/51420df8e5abe5b7a0b4e05781bc/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=400d83d40dae53a2c7fddf5895ad248f99ae9844468dae17b3e486c63258599a&req=diQvF8t%2FnIJaWvMW1HO4zflQ7Mala1bBDggfcRWq0%2FCtSLig9r6eCcfEa3Rj%0AUZrzV6bjTjDn0eKivCs%3D%0A)

Your custom group will now appear under the default groups

* * *

**Editing a Group**
-------------------

To edit a group, click the **Edit Icon (pencil icon)** next to the group name and select **URL List** from the modal popup to your right. From there, you can view and modify the URLs in the group.

_Note: Default groups cannot be edited._

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1592381726/b06ed84a21e0a7b1904b09c4ef9b/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=bb375d899456d7241e1b6083a6f7a11d533bc38b8d0382a6f1807ff6b50c7d1e&req=dSUuFMp2nIZdX%2FMW1HO4zfOnyiWoRW7Gp6%2B2GK66F5mT2lszbJ9N6Q2FpCsI%0AB2gk%2Bs3ByzRG3KNod0w%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1592381726/b06ed84a21e0a7b1904b09c4ef9b/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=bb375d899456d7241e1b6083a6f7a11d533bc38b8d0382a6f1807ff6b50c7d1e&req=dSUuFMp2nIZdX%2FMW1HO4zfOnyiWoRW7Gp6%2B2GK66F5mT2lszbJ9N6Q2FpCsI%0AB2gk%2Bs3ByzRG3KNod0w%3D%0A)

Understanding and Using Interactive Mode on Heatmap
===================================================

Interactive Mode, dynamic elements, real-time tracking, drop-down menus, pop-ups, UX insights, Heatmap.com, website optimization, conversion

October 21, 2024

Heatmap.com's Interactive Mode is an advanced analytics feature that provides dynamic and real-time visual representations of user engagement on your website. This tool extends beyond traditional static heatmaps by allowing you to see how users interact with every element of your website, including dynamic and interactive components. Interactive Mode is particularly useful for business owners, UX professionals, and web designers looking to gain deep insights into user behavior and improve website functionality and design.  
​

With Interactive Mode, you can track interactions with elements such as drop-down menus, hamburger menus, and pop-ups that are typically challenging to analyze with standard heatmaps. The feature also allows for segmentation and filtering of data based on device type, geographic location, user behavior, and more, enabling highly targeted analysis. By leveraging these insights, you can optimize element placement, content strategy, and overall site navigation to enhance user experience and drive conversions.

# Understanding Heatmap.com Metrics | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023912-understanding-heatmap-com-metrics#main-content)

Understanding Heatmap.com Metrics
=================================

Metrics

October 21, 2024

**Understanding Heatmap.com Metrics**

Heatmap.com provides several key metrics to help you analyze your website's performance. This guide explains what each metric means and how to use it effectively.

**Clicks**

**Definition:** The total number of times users have clicked on a specific element.

Use: Measure engagement with different page elements. Higher click counts generally indicate popular or important features.

**Purchases**

Definition: The number of completed transactions associated with a particular element.

Use: Identify which elements are most effective at driving sales.

**Revenue**

**Definition:** The total monetary value generated from purchases associated with an element.

**Use**: Understand which elements contribute most to your bottom line.

**Avg. Order Value (AOV)**

**Definition:** The average amount spent per purchase associated with an element.

**Calculation:** Total Revenue / Number of Purchases

Use: Identify elements that lead to higher-value purchases.

**Conversion Rate**

Definition: The percentage of clicks on an element that result in a purchase.

**Calculation:** (Purchases / Clicks) x 100

**Use:** Measure how effective an element is at turning interest into sales.

**Visibility**

**Definition:** The percentage of users who see a particular element on your page.

**Use:** Understand how many visitors are exposed to each element, helping you prioritize placement and design.

**Rev. per Click**

**Definition:** The average revenue generated each time an element is clicked.

**Calculation:** Total Revenue / Number of Clicks

**Use:** Compare the monetary value of different clickable elements, regardless of their position or visibility.

**Rev. per Session**

**Definition:** The average revenue generated per user session that includes interaction with a specific element.

**Calculation:** Total Revenue / Number of Sessions involving the element

**Use:** Understand the overall impact of an element on session value, even if it's not directly involved in a purchase.

**Using These Metrics Together**

While each metric provides valuable insights on its own, combining them can give you a more comprehensive view of your website's performance. For example:

\- An element with high clicks but low purchases might be misleading or not meeting user expectations.

\- High revenue but low conversion rate could indicate a few high-value purchases skewing the data.

\- Elements with high visibility but low clicks may need redesign or repositioning.

Remember, always consider these metrics in the context of your specific business goals and user behavior patterns.

Need more help understanding your metrics? Contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

The basics
----------

**What is the Attention Map?**

The Attention Map shows where visitors actually pay attention on a page — not just how far they scrolled or where they clicked. It measures, for every 5% band of the page and for the key elements on it, how long the content was genuinely in view, how long the mouse lingered there, how long people hesitated before clicking, and how much revenue came from the sessions that engaged.

**How is this different from a scroll map or a click map?**

A scroll map tells you how far down the page someone got. A click map tells you where they acted. Neither tells you what held them. Most of what happens on a page — reading, comparing, hesitating, losing interest — never becomes a click. The Attention Map measures that middle layer.

It also separates two things scroll depth blends together: how many people _reached_ a section, and how many of them _engaged_ with it. A footer only 4% of visitors reach can still be the most engaging block on the page for the people who get there.

**What's the difference between the Measured and AI Prediction tabs?**

*   **Measured** is real behaviour from your real visitors.
    
*   **AI Prediction** is a model's forecast of where attention will land, based on the visual design of the page alone. No traffic required.
    
*   **Compare** puts them side by side with a shared depth highlighter.
    

Measured tells you what happened. Prediction tells you what the design is _inviting_ people to look at. The gap between them is usually the interesting part.

**What do I use it for?**

Three common jobs:

1.  Finding content that earns attention but is buried too far down the page.
    
2.  Finding elements that people look at for a long time before acting — usually a copy or clarity problem, not a design one.
    
3.  Deciding what to test next, with evidence rather than opinion.
    

**Do I need to install anything new?**

No. The Attention Map runs on your existing Heatmap installation. There's no second snippet and no tagging work required to get started.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2643637708/241e3721a4caad1ce66852aa2c02/Screenshot+2026-09-01+at+8_54_13%E2%80%AFAM.png?expires=1789486200&signature=55b4182587dd5e1326257e8d0ca23ffcb75d7a3dbdd60f411f2dc3c125e07368&req=diYjFc99moZfUfMW1HO4zSplfKflYwlnBh50JMZdyeA%2BL0zwnW55oF%2BHnGBP%0AKDGslztfuJlX9xq8%2Beo%3D%0A)](https://www.heatmap.com/pricing)

* * *

What it measures
----------------

**What is a depth zone?**

The page is divided into horizontal bands, 5% of the page height each — 20 bands from the top of the page to the bottom. Every metric in the depth view is reported per band. Wider bands (10%, 20%, 25%) are available for very long pages.

**What do Reach % and Attention % mean?**

*   **Reach %** — how many visitors got this far down the page, as a share of the most-reached zone on the page.
    
*   **Attention %** — of the visitors who reached that zone, the share who had it genuinely in view for at least 2 seconds.
    

Reach is about position. Attention is about whether the content did anything once it was seen. A zone with high reach and low attention is content people scroll straight past.

**What is dwell?**

Seconds that a zone or element was visible in the viewport, on a visible browser tab, with the visitor active. Time in a background tab doesn't count. Neither does time after the visitor goes idle — accrual pauses after 5 minutes of no scrolling, clicking, or typing, and resumes when they come back.

**What is float?**

Seconds the mouse cursor hovered over that zone or element. On desktop, cursor position is a reasonable proxy for reading position — people tend to park the mouse near what they're looking at.

**What is hesitancy? What's a bad number?**

Hesitancy is how long someone hovered on an element before clicking it, measured only among people who did click. It's reported as a median and a maximum.

There's no universal threshold, but the shape of the signal is consistent: low hesitancy means the element was obvious, high hesitancy means people had to think. High hesitancy on a CTA almost always points at the copy or the offer — the button isn't communicating clearly enough what happens next.

The companion metric is **fast-click %**: the share of clickers who clicked within 3 seconds. High fast-click plus low hesitancy is a healthy CTA.

**Which elements get tracked? Can I choose them?**

Up to 10 elements per page (12 maximum). They're detected automatically and classified as calls-to-action, media, or content blocks.

You can also mark specific elements yourself by adding a `data-hm-watch` attribute to them in your theme, with a name of your choosing. Tagged elements keep the name you give them, which makes them easier to find in reports.

**How does an element count as "seen"?**

An element has to be at least 40% visible before it starts accruing time. A zone has to overlap the viewport by at least 5%. This is deliberate — it stops content that merely clipped the edge of the screen from being counted as viewed.

**What does the revenue column on an element mean?**

Revenue from sessions that engaged with that element and purchased in the same session, plus purchase count and revenue per session. It's same-session attribution, so treat it as "elements that appear on the path to purchase" rather than proof of causation. A split test is still what proves causation.

**What is active vs. open time?**

Two numbers side by side: the median time the page was actually visible and being used, versus the median total time the tab was open. The gap is how much of your reported "time on page" is real. Pages where the two numbers diverge sharply usually have visitors parking the tab and coming back later — high time on page that isn't engagement.

* * *

Reading the data
----------------

**What are insight cards?**

Generated summaries of what stands out on the page. Six types:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Card | What it flags |
| Hidden gem | A zone with high attention but low reach — good content, buried too deep |
| Move-up candidate | Content that would likely earn more if it sat higher on the page |
| Hesitancy hotspot | An element people hover a long time before clicking |
| Active vs. open time | A large gap between real attention and reported time on page |
| Money zone | The depth band most associated with purchasing sessions |
| Revenue driver | The element most associated with purchasing sessions |

They're a starting point for a hypothesis, not a verdict. Confirm anything surprising against the underlying numbers before you act on it.

**Why doesn't an element I care about appear in the report?**

Most likely one of three reasons:

1.  **Not enough viewers.** Elements need at least 5 distinct viewers before they're reported. Below that the numbers are noise.
    
2.  **Not detected.** It wasn't picked up as a call-to-action, media, or content block. Add a `data-hm-watch` attribute to track it explicitly.
    
3.  **Element cap.** Only the top elements on the page are tracked, up to 12.
    

**Can I filter the data?**

Yes — date range, device, new vs. returning visitors, buyers vs. non-buyers, traffic source, and country.

**Can I see attention for buyers only?**

Yes, and it's one of the most useful things in the report. Buyer reach and buyer attention are reported per zone, so you can see which sections of the page the people who actually purchased spent time on. Comparing buyers against everyone tells you which content is doing persuasive work and which is just occupying space.

* * *

AI Prediction
-------------

**How does the prediction work?**

We capture a full-page screenshot of the page and run it through a predictive attention model. The model returns a predicted attention intensity for every point on the page — displayed as an Attention score from 0 to 100 — plus predicted attention by depth, and heatmap, focus, and contrast views of the page. `[[VENDOR-ATTRIBUTION]]`

**Is this eye-tracking?**

No. It's a model trained to predict where human attention goes based on the visual properties of a design — contrast, size, position, faces, text density. No visitors are involved. That's the point: you can run it on a page that has no traffic yet, including a page that isn't live.

**When measured and predicted disagree, which one is right?**

Both, about different things. The prediction describes what the design pulls the eye toward. The measured data describes what your actual visitors, with their actual intent, did.

The two useful patterns:

*   **Predicted high, measured low** — the design is shouting about something visitors don't care about. Usually a relevance or messaging problem.
    
*   **Predicted low, measured high** — visitors are hunting for something the design is hiding. Usually the fastest win on the page: make the thing they're already looking for easier to find.
    

**Why does the prediction look different from my live page?**

The screenshot is taken with cookie and consent banners suppressed and at a single viewport, so the captured page may differ from what you'd see yourself — particularly on pages with personalization, geo-specific content, or an active A/B test.

**Can I run the prediction on a page that isn't live yet?**

Not in this release — prediction runs against a URL we can reach. Pre-launch design review is on the roadmap.

* * *

Data accuracy and privacy
-------------------------

**How soon does data appear, and how often does it update?**

Attention data begins appearing within a couple of hours of a site being enabled, and updates hourly after that. It isn't a live view.

**Why don't the depth percentages match my scroll depth report?**

Because the Attention Map only aggregates visitors who saw a comparable version of the page. Pages vary in height between visitors — A/B test variants, geo-specific blocks, lazy-loaded sections — and averaging a visitor who saw a 4,000px page with one who saw a 12,000px page makes the depth percentages meaningless. So the depth view keeps pageviews whose page height falls within ±25% of the median for that page and excludes the rest.

The result is a depth map you can trust for positional decisions, at the cost of not matching a raw scroll number exactly. Both are correct; they're answering different questions.

**Why are hover and hesitancy near zero on mobile?**

Float and hesitancy are cursor metrics, and touch devices have no cursor. On mobile, use dwell, reach, attention %, and clicks. Read hover-based metrics as desktop signals only.

**What happens on pages that change height as they load?**

When a page grows substantially past its initial height — lazy-loaded sections, infinite scroll — the depth grid is locked to a stable reference height so that zone boundaries mean the same thing for every visitor. Without this, the same pixel would land in different zones for different people and the depth map would be unreadable.

**How are rage clicks and bots handled?**

Pageviews with an abnormal burst of clicks in a short window are flagged so they can be excluded from analysis rather than distorting engagement numbers.

**What data does this collect? Is it privacy-safe?**

The Attention Map records timing and interaction data — how long regions and elements were in view, cursor position over the page, and click timing. It doesn't capture form contents, keystrokes, or personal information. Everything is reported in aggregate.

Visitors who should not be tracked at all can be excluded using the standard Heatmap do-not-track flag, which suppresses attention collection entirely for that visitor.

**Does this slow my site down?**

No measurable impact. The tracker samples once a second and sends compact batched updates rather than a stream of events. Tracker performance overhead is tested against live production sites as part of every release.

**Does this depend on session recording?**

No. Attention collection runs on every pageview independently of whether that visit is being recorded, so your attention data is complete even when session recording samples a visit out.

* * *

Access and troubleshooting
--------------------------

**How do I get access?**

The Attention Map is rolling out progressively across accounts. `[[ACCESS-PATH]]`

**I've been enabled but I see no data.**

Check in this order:

1.  Has it been at least two hours since enablement?
    
2.  Is the page you're looking at one that actually gets traffic in the selected date range?
    
3.  Is the do-not-track flag set on your site?
    
4.  Are your filters excluding everything — a narrow date range plus a device plus a source will empty most reports.
    

If all four are clear, contact [Support@heatmap.com](mailto:Support@heatmap.com)
 with the site and page URL.

**A number looks impossibly high or doubled.**

Report it to [Support@heatmap.com](mailto:Support@heatmap.com)
 with the page URL, date range, and filters applied. Include a screenshot if you can — it makes diagnosis much faster.

**How far back does the data go?**

Attention data starts accruing when your site is enabled. It isn't backfilled from before that point.

* * *

Need help?
----------

If you have questions or run into any issues while using Heatmap, our support team is here to help. Contact us anytime at [Support@heatmap.com](mailto:Support@heatmap.com)
.

# How Revenue and Metrics are Calculated | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023929-how-revenue-and-metrics-are-calculated#main-content)

How Revenue and Metrics are Calculated
======================================

Revenue, metrics, calculations

October 21, 2024

**How Revenue and Metrics are Calculated**

Understanding how Heatmap.com calculates revenue and other key metrics is crucial for making informed decisions about your website's performance. This article explains our calculation methods for two primary metrics: Revenue Per Click and Revenue Per Session.

**Important Notes on Revenue Attribution**

1\. **Aggregated Model**: Heatmap.com uses an aggregated model for tracking revenue per element. This means:

\- If a user clicks multiple elements before making a purchase, the full revenue is attributed to each clicked element.

\- Example: If a user clicks 10 elements before making a $100 purchase, each of those 10 elements is attributed $100 in revenue.

2\. **Session-Based**: Revenue is calculated on a per-session basis, not per user. A single user may have multiple sessions, each counted separately.

3\. **Last-Click Attribution**: For conversion tracking, we use a last-click attribution model. The last element clicked before a purchase gets credit for the conversion.

**Using These Metrics**

\- Use Revenue Per Click to identify your highest-performing individual elements.

\- Use Revenue Per Session to understand overall page performance and compare similar elements.

\- Always consider these metrics in context with other data points, such as total clicks, total sessions, and conversion rates.

Remember, while these metrics provide valuable insights, they should be part of a comprehensive analysis of your website's performance. Always test changes based on these metrics to ensure they truly improve your site's overall performance and user experience.

For more detailed analysis or custom metric calculations, please contact our support team.

# Where to Download Invoices for Your Heatmap Subscription? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024003-where-to-download-invoices-for-your-heatmap-subscription#main-content)

Where to Download Invoices for Your Heatmap Subscription?
=========================================================

download invoices, Heatmap subscription, invoice history, billing address update, payment details, PDF invoices, account details, support

October 21, 2024

**Where to Download Invoices for Your Heatmap Subscription?**

Accessing and downloading invoices for your heatmap subscription is simple. Follow these steps:

1\. Log in to your heatmap account.

2\. Click on "Payments" in the left sidebar.

3\. Scroll down to the "Invoice History" section.

4\. Locate the invoice you want to download.

5\. Click the download icon (usually a downward arrow) next to the desired invoice.

6\. The invoice will download as a PDF file to your device.

You can repeat this process for any invoice in your history.

\*\*Updating Account Details or Billing Address:\*\*

If you need to change any account details or the billing address on your invoice, please contact our support team. They can update this information for you to ensure your invoices are accurate.

Need older invoices or have questions? Contact our support team via chat or email [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

Introduction to Heatmap
=======================

Introduction, heatmap.com, key features

October 21, 2024

**Introduction to Heatmap**

Heatmap is a powerful analytics tool designed to help you understand and optimize your website's user experience. Unlike traditional analytics that provide numerical data, Heatmap offers visual representations of user behavior on your website.

Key Features:

*   Visual Behavior Map:
    
*   Revenue-Based Insights
    
*   heatmapAI
    
*   Data Table Exports
    
*   Compare Mode
    
*   Site Speed Tracking
    
*   JavaScript Error Tracking
    
*   IP Blocking
    
*   Custom Filtering
    

Heatmap goes beyond just showing clicks and scrolls. It provides valuable revenue data for every element on your website, allowing you to make data-driven decisions to improve your conversion rates and overall user experience.
