# How to Find Your Tracking Snippet for Reinstallation | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024021-how-to-find-your-tracking-snippet-for-reinstallation#main-content)

How to Find Your Tracking Snippet for Reinstallation
====================================================

reinstall snippet, Heatmap.com, view snippet, website tracking, HTML installation, revenue snippet, e-commerce tracking, CMS guides, support

October 21, 2024

**How to Find Your Tracking Snippet for Reinstallation**

If you need to reinstall your heatmap tracking snippet, you can easily access it from your account. Follow these simple steps:

1\. Log in to your heatmap.com dashboard.

2\. Navigate to the "All Websites" section in the left sidebar.

3\. Find the website you need the snippet for in the list.

4\. Click the "View Snippet" button next to the website name.

5\. A modal window will open, displaying your unique tracking snippet.

From here, you can copy the snippet and paste it into your website's HTML, typically just before the closing </head> tag.

Remember, for full functionality, ensure you've also installed the revenue snippet if you're tracking e-commerce data.

If you're using a content management system like Shopify or WordPress, refer to our platform-specific installation guides for detailed instructions.

Need help? Don't hesitate to contact our support team through the chat widget or at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

# How to Install and Use the Heatmap Chrome Extension | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15859877-how-to-install-and-use-the-heatmap-chrome-extension#main-content)

How to Install and Use the Heatmap Chrome Extension
===================================================

A Chrome extension that provides another way to view your heatmap pages directly from your url bypassing the content security restrictions from Shopify and Cloudflare.

July 10, 2026

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15859877-how-to-install-and-use-the-heatmap-chrome-extension#h_a930cfd626)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15859877-how-to-install-and-use-the-heatmap-chrome-extension#h_08b699d8f8)

The Heatmap Chrome extension provides a reliable way to view your heatmap pages when the standard page preview is affected by proxy or rendering issues.  
With the extension installed, your website pages should load directly in Chrome without rendering problems, 504s, local\_rate\_limited errors, connection error messages or Shopify Cloudflare restrictions for third party apps.

  
With the extension installed, you can open your live website directly in Chrome, scan the page, and click on tracked elements to view their performance data in the panel on the right.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526694754/fe94be7c4f5381aaae0d2a4554e2/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=bc30da29a02063835b9f407ad70c47c4094a448de6fd7e51a4c56c9e0abe6c2e&req=diUlEM93mYZaXfMW1HO4zeUweyXBATB6KN6LEIYXQqkdG50JMWruOZKOmD%2Fe%0A%2FrS7HTrVw%2FrzjzdtsJc%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526694754/fe94be7c4f5381aaae0d2a4554e2/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=bc30da29a02063835b9f407ad70c47c4094a448de6fd7e51a4c56c9e0abe6c2e&req=diUlEM93mYZaXfMW1HO4zeUweyXBATB6KN6LEIYXQqkdG50JMWruOZKOmD%2Fe%0A%2FrS7HTrVw%2FrzjzdtsJc%3D%0A)

* * *

  
**How to Install the Extension**
===================================

1.  Log in to your Heatmap account and click the Chrome extension link provided in the platform.
    
2.  Download and install the **Heatmap Chrome Extension or** directly from the Google Chrome store.
    
    [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526702331/4573f1da9accc914b601aba74680/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=bb2eb705ecd1f45846ed16477119a4bdc7671f21567220bba7f0038f13e1ed6c&req=diUlEM5%2Bn4JcWPMW1HO4zT7AbM51yENmMeFOWaLv6BdBfg3oHLijVJOOk5x6%0ATvQL%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526702331/4573f1da9accc914b601aba74680/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=bb2eb705ecd1f45846ed16477119a4bdc7671f21567220bba7f0038f13e1ed6c&req=diUlEM5%2Bn4JcWPMW1HO4zT7AbM51yENmMeFOWaLv6BdBfg3oHLijVJOOk5x6%0ATvQL%0A)
    
3.  Once installed, open your live website.
    
4.  Click the Heatmap extension icon in your Chrome toolbar and log in to your Heatmap account.
    
    [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526709700/0169cc85b5d633b1866ffa9d759e/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=b2978f1b6879e6be7e17546761f4acfacc8ce6df0652d9016c6c7efed37e8ee0&req=diUlEM5%2BlIZfWfMW1HO4zeqZ%2Bh1HazzXmsVLzrR4rWT4qaWgG7OVQ3lLkj%2B6%0ArR5Q%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526709700/0169cc85b5d633b1866ffa9d759e/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=b2978f1b6879e6be7e17546761f4acfacc8ce6df0652d9016c6c7efed37e8ee0&req=diUlEM5%2BlIZfWfMW1HO4zeqZ%2Bh1HazzXmsVLzrR4rWT4qaWgG7OVQ3lLkj%2B6%0ArR5Q%0A)
    
5.  Select **Heatmap** and allow the extension to scan and access the current page.
    
    [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526717225/78983bab96d1e0fed3d695887634/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=0da9b3254d86801bd5b0bf815ae6acb9f3f3d21afef8f9b698f74319a078bcdf&req=diUlEM5%2FmoNdXPMW1HO4zaiAJy6khHNrmN4DpksTDbk4v7jBmA%2FJXW%2BeW4yo%0Apsna%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526717225/78983bab96d1e0fed3d695887634/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=0da9b3254d86801bd5b0bf815ae6acb9f3f3d21afef8f9b698f74319a078bcdf&req=diUlEM5%2FmoNdXPMW1HO4zaiAJy6khHNrmN4DpksTDbk4v7jBmA%2FJXW%2BeW4yo%0Apsna%0A)
    
6.  Click any tracked element on the page to view its related performance data in the panel on the right.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526762300/dea51be2ed82bebb5edc5cf609ad/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=f5f1d306f8c778b2725cfcd1749bb145de0e8627b93972ea3c611c4e97342e11&req=diUlEM54n4JfWfMW1HO4zbZGFdJQ6LSru1hv8GeDpH63mMvpmFCBwgcuB%2F0d%0A3vZUKzgyY7%2BtRnULl%2BU%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2526762300/dea51be2ed82bebb5edc5cf609ad/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=f5f1d306f8c778b2725cfcd1749bb145de0e8627b93972ea3c611c4e97342e11&req=diUlEM54n4JfWfMW1HO4zbZGFdJQ6LSru1hv8GeDpH63mMvpmFCBwgcuB%2F0d%0A3vZUKzgyY7%2BtRnULl%2BU%3D%0A)

* * *

**What the extension helps with**  
The Heatmap Chrome extension allows you to:

*   View pages that may not load correctly through the standard Heatmap proxy.
    
*   Review heatmap data directly on your live website.
    
*   Interact with menus, buttons, and other page elements while reviewing data.
    
*   Click individual elements to view their related metrics.
    
*   Continue analyzing your pages while our team investigates any underlying proxy issues.
    

**Important Note**

The extension only works on websites that have been properly installed and configured in Heatmap with an active subscription.

Analytics displaying session and revenue data will not work on random websites or pages that have not been connected to the Heatmap platform.

**Need Help?**
--------------

After installing the extension, test it on your website and confirm that your pages and element data are loading correctly.

If you experience any issues, contact our support team [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 and we’ll be happy to assist.

How to Access the Heatmap API and Connect Heatmap MCP to Claude
===============================================================

This guide walks you through creating API keys in Heatmap and connecting Heatmap MCP to Claude.

July 7, 2026

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15862268-how-to-access-the-heatmap-api-and-connect-heatmap-mcp-to-claude#h_893bde197c)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15862268-how-to-access-the-heatmap-api-and-connect-heatmap-mcp-to-claude#h_60761558be)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15862268-how-to-access-the-heatmap-api-and-connect-heatmap-mcp-to-claude#h_6c6fc6e74e)

**Create an API Key in Heatmap**
================================

To access the Heatmap API:

1.  Request access by reaching out to [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
    
2.  Log out of your Heatmap account, then log back in.

# FAQ: Heatmap.com's Interactive Mode | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023941-faq-heatmap-com-s-interactive-mode#main-content)

FAQ: Heatmap.com's Interactive Mode
===================================

Interactive Mode, dynamic elements, real-time tracking, drop-down menus, pop-ups,UX insights, Heatmap.com, website optimization, conversions

March 12, 2025

**What is Interactive Mode in Heatmap.com?**  
Interactive Mode is an advanced feature that provides real-time, dynamic visual representations of user engagement on your website. It goes beyond traditional static heatmaps by capturing interactions with dynamic elements like drop-down menus, pop-ups, and hamburger menus.  
​

**Who benefits from using Interactive Mode?**  
Business owners, UX professionals, and web designers can use Interactive Mode to gain deeper insights into user behavior and improve website design and functionality.  
​

**What types of user interactions can be tracked in Interactive Mode?**  
Interactive Mode tracks user interactions with dynamic components such as:

*   Drop-down menus
    
*   Hamburger menus
    
*   Sliders
    
*   Pop-ups  
    This tool helps analyze elements that are typically difficult to track with standard heatmaps.
    

**How can Interactive Mode improve my website?**  
By analyzing user interactions with key elements, you can optimize element placement, content strategy, and site navigation, which helps enhance user experience and drive conversions.  
​  
Interactive Mode lets you interact with elements on the page, but it doesn’t support actions that redirect to a different URL, like adding items to a cart.  
This is due to how Interactive Mode was designed to work—keeping everything on the same page without redirection.

October 21, 2024

**How to Add a New Payment Method to Your Account?**

Adding a new payment method to your heatmap account is quick and easy. Follow these simple steps:

1\. Log in to your heatmap account.

2\. Click on "Payment" in the left sidebar.

3\. Look for the "Add Card" button on the right side of the page.

4\. Click "Add Card" to open the payment form.

5\. Enter your card details:

\- Cardholder name

\- Card number

\- Expiration date

\- CVV (security code)

6\. Review the information to ensure it's correct.

7\. Click "Save" to add your new payment method.

Your new card will now be available for future payments and subscriptions.

**Overview**
============

Custom Events allow you to track specific user interactions and behaviors on your website that go beyond standard pageviews and clicks. With Custom Events, you can measure actions like button clicks, video plays, page views, and any other custom interactions that matter to your business.

**What are Custom Events?**
---------------------------

Custom Events are user-defined tracking points that capture specific actions visitors take on your website. Unlike automatic tracking that records all clicks and pageviews, Custom Events let you focus on the interactions that are most important to your conversion goals and user experience optimization.

**Benefits of Custom Events**
-----------------------------

**Targeted Tracking**: Focus on the specific user actions that drive your business objectives rather than sorting through all generic click data.

**Better Analysis**: Understand how users interact with key elements like CTA buttons, form fields, video content, and interactive features. You'll be able to use these insights to filter through the rest of your data.

**Simple Creation**: Track virtually any element of your website by grabbing the CSS selector and wait for the data to roll in.

* * *

**Setting Up Custom Events**
============================

* * *

**How to Find CSS Selectors**
=============================

Finding the right CSS selector is the key to setting up Custom Events correctly. Here's a step-by-step guide:

**Step 1: Open Your Browser's Developer Tools**
-----------------------------------------------

**Chrome, Edge, or Brave:**

*   Right-click on the element you want to track (button, link, form, etc.)
    
*   Select **Inspect** from the menu
    
*   This opens the Developer Tools panel
    

**Firefox:**

*   Right-click on the element
    
*   Select **Inspect Element**
    

**Safari:**

*   First enable Developer Tools: Safari menu → Preferences → Advanced → Check "Show Develop menu"
    
*   Right-click on the element
    
*   Select **Inspect Element**
    

**Step 2: Locate the Element in the HTML**
------------------------------------------

Once Developer Tools are open, you'll see the HTML code. The element you clicked should be highlighted. It might look something like this:

html

<button class="cta-button primary" id="signup-btn">Get Started</button>

**Step 3: Identify the Best Selector**
--------------------------------------

Look for identifiers in this order of preference:

**1\. ID (Best option if available)**

*   Look for id="something"
    
*   CSS Selector format: #signup-btn
    
*   IDs are unique and won't accidentally track multiple elements
    

**2\. Unique Class Name**

*   Look for class="something"
    
*   CSS Selector format: .cta-button or .signup-button
    
*   Make sure the class is specific to that element type
    

**3\. Combination of Classes**

*   CSS Selector format: .cta-button.primary
    
*   Use when single classes aren't unique enough
    

**4\. Element with Attribute**

*   CSS Selector format: button\[type="submit"\]
    
*   Useful for form buttons or links with specific attributes
    

**Step 4: Copy the Selector**
-----------------------------

**Chrome/Edge Method (Easiest):**

1.  In the Developer Tools, make sure the element is still highlighted
    
2.  Right-click on the highlighted HTML line
    
3.  Select **Copy** → **Copy selector**
    
4.  Paste this into the CSS Selector field in Heatmap.com
    

**Manual Method:**

1.  Identify the ID or class from the HTML
    
2.  Write the selector yourself using the rules above
    
3.  Test it (see Step 5)
    

**Step 5: Test Your Selector**
------------------------------

Before saving your Custom Event, test that your selector works:

1.  In Developer Tools, press Ctrl+F (Windows) or Cmd+F (Mac)
    
2.  Paste your CSS selector in the search box
    
3.  The browser will highlight matching elements
    
4.  **Important**: Make sure only ONE element is highlighted (or only the specific elements you want to track)
    
5.  If multiple unwanted elements are highlighted, you need a more specific selector
    

**Common Selector Examples**
----------------------------

**Tracking a specific button by ID:**

#signup-button

**Tracking all "Add to Cart" buttons with the same class:**

.add-to-cart-btn

**Tracking a form submission button:**

form#contact-form button\[type="submit"\]

**Tracking a navigation link:**

nav a\[href="/pricing"\]

**Tracking any element with specific text (use carefully):**

button:contains("Download")

**Selector Best Practices**
---------------------------

**Be Specific Enough**: Your selector should only match the element(s) you want to track. Too broad and you'll track unwanted clicks.

**Avoid Overly Complex Selectors**: Selectors like div > div > div.class > span can break if your website structure changes. Use IDs or specific classes when possible.

**Use Stable Identifiers**: Choose IDs or classes that are unlikely to change. Avoid classes like .btn-1 or .element-a7f2 that look auto-generated.

**Test on Multiple Pages**: If your element appears on different pages, test that your selector works consistently across all of them.

* * *

**Event Types**
===============

### **Click Events**

Track when users click on specific elements like buttons, links, images, or any clickable element. This is the most common Custom Event type.

**Use for:**

*   CTA button clicks
    
*   Navigation menu items
    
*   Download links
    
*   Image clicks
    
*   Form submissions (when tracking the submit button)
    

### **Page View Events**

Track when users view a page that contains a specific element. Useful for tracking exposure to important content or reaching specific sections.

**Use for:**

*   Seeing if users reach important pages
    
*   Tracking visibility of special offers
    
*   Measuring engagement with specific content sections
    
*   Funnel stage completions
    

* * *

**Viewing Custom Event Data**
=============================

**Event Log and Troubleshooting**
---------------------------------

After creating a Custom Event, you can monitor whether it's firing correctly:

1.  Go to **Settings** → **Custom Events**
    
2.  Click on **Event Log**
    
3.  Watch for your event to appear as users interact with your site
    

**Important**: It takes approximately 30 minutes for event data to start populating in the Event Log. This is a great way to verify your CSS selector is working correctly before relying on the data for analysis.

**Custom Events Dashboard**
---------------------------

In the Custom Events section of Settings, you'll see an overview of all your events with key metrics:

*   **Count**: Total number of times the event has fired
    
*   **Sessions**: Number of unique sessions where the event occurred
    
*   **Counts per Session**: Average number of times the event fires per session
    

### **Viewing Individual Event Reports:**

1.  Click on any Custom Event in the list
    
2.  You'll see a detailed report showing:
    
    *   The three metrics above over your selected time period
        
    *   A visualization of event trends
        
    
3.  From this view you can:
    
    *   **Adjust the date range** to analyze different time periods
        
    *   **Edit the CSS selector** if you need to refine what's being tracked
        
    *   **Update the event name**
        
    

**Filtering with Custom Events**
--------------------------------

The real power of Custom Events comes from using them as filters across all Heatmap features. Once an event is created and collecting data, you can filter by it to focus your analysis.

### **Using Custom Events in Heatmaps**

1.  Open **Heatmaps** from the main navigation
    
2.  Click the **Filters** tab
    
3.  Select your Custom Event from the dropdown
    
4.  The heatmap will now show only data from sessions where that event occurred
    

**Interpretation tip**: This helps you understand how users who perform specific actions (like clicking your CTA) behave differently on your pages compared to all visitors.

### **Using Custom Events in Recordings**

1.  Open **Recordings**
    
2.  Click the **Filters** tab
    
3.  Select your Custom Event
    
4.  You'll see only recordings where users triggered that event
    

**Interpretation tip**: Watch recordings of users who completed important actions to understand their journey, or filter by events that _should_ happen but have low counts to see where users are getting stuck.

### **Using Custom Events in Funnels**

1.  Open **Funnels** or create a new funnel
    
2.  Click the **Filters** tab
    
3.  Apply your Custom Event as a filter
    
4.  The funnel will show customer journeys only for users who triggered that event
    

**Interpretation tip**: Compare funnel performance between users who engaged with certain elements (like watching a demo video) versus those who didn't, to measure the impact of that engagement on conversions.

### **Using Custom Events in Analytics**

1.  Open **Analytics**
    
2.  Navigate to the **Filters** tab
    
3.  Select one or more Custom Events
    
4.  All analytics data will be filtered to sessions containing those events
    

**Interpretation tip**: Segment your traffic data by Custom Events to understand which pages, sources, or devices correlate with your most valuable user actions.

**Combining Multiple Filters**
------------------------------

You can combine Custom Events with other filters like:

*   Device type (Desktop, Mobile, Tablet)
    
*   Traffic source (Direct, Organic, Referral, etc.)
    

This allows for powerful segmentation.

**Best Practices**
------------------

**Use Clear Naming Conventions**: Choose event names that are descriptive and consistent across your team.

**Don't Over-Track**: Focus on meaningful interactions rather than tracking every possible action. Too many events can make analysis overwhelming.

**Include Relevant Properties**: Add context to your events with properties that will help with future analysis.

**Test Before Deploying**: Always test your Custom Events in a development environment before pushing to production.

**Document Your Events**: Keep a reference guide of all Custom Events, their purpose, and where they're implemented.

**Common Use Cases**
--------------------

### **E-commerce**

*   Add to cart clicks
    
*   Wishlist additions
    
*   Product quick view opens
    
*   Size/color selection changes
    

### **SaaS Applications**

*   Feature usage tracking
    
*   Upgrade button clicks
    
*   Trial signup completions
    
*   Onboarding step completions
    

### **Content Sites**

*   Video play/pause/complete
    
*   Article scroll depth milestones
    
*   Social share button clicks
    
*   Newsletter subscription submissions
    

### **Lead Generation**

*   Contact form submissions
    
*   Phone number clicks
    
*   Live chat initiations
    
*   Resource download clicks
    

* * *

**Troubleshooting**
===================

If your Custom Event isn't working as expected, here's how to diagnose the issue:

**Check the Event Log**
-----------------------

1.  Go to **Settings** → **Custom Events** → **Event Log**
    
2.  Wait at least 30 minutes after creating the event for data to appear
    
3.  Interact with the element on your site that should trigger the event
    
4.  Refresh the Event Log to see if the event appears
    

**If the event is firing in the Event Log**: Your Custom Event is set up correctly and data should start appearing in your reports within 30 minutes.

**If the event is NOT firing in the Event Log**: Your CSS selector likely isn't matching the correct element.

**Verify Your CSS Selector**
----------------------------

The most common issue is an incorrect CSS selector. Double-check:

1.  Open your website and use browser Developer Tools to inspect the element
    
2.  Verify the selector you entered matches the element exactly
    
3.  Test the selector in Developer Tools (press Ctrl+F or Cmd+F in the Elements panel and paste your selector)
    
4.  Make sure only the intended element(s) are highlighted
    
5.  If needed, update the CSS selector in your Custom Event settings
    

### **Common Selector Issues**

*   **Dynamically generated:** Selectors that contain numbers are often dynamically generated and can limit tracking. We recommend simplifying the selector.
    
*   **Element ID or class changed**: Website updates may have modified the HTML structure
    
*   **Selector too specific**: Overly complex selectors may not match across different pages
    
*   **Selector too broad**: May be matching multiple unintended elements
    
*   **Wrong selector format**: Missing # for IDs or . for classes
    

**Still Not Working?**
----------------------

If you've verified your CSS selector is correct and the event still isn't firing in the Event Log, please contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
. Our team will need to review the issue internally to identify and resolve any technical problems with event tracking.

* * *

**Need Help?**
--------------

If you have questions about setting up Custom Events or need assistance with implementation, contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 or visit our Help Center for additional resources.

# How to Purchase a Subscription and Add a New Website | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024011-how-to-purchase-a-subscription-and-add-a-new-website#main-content)

How to Purchase a Subscription and Add a New Website
====================================================

purchase subscription, add website, Heatmap.com, Pro plan, Enterprise plan, monthly billing, annual billing, payment details, tracking snippet

October 21, 2024

**How to Purchase a Subscription and Add a New Website**

Follow these steps to purchase a subscription and start tracking a new website with heatmap:

1\. Log in to your heatmap.com account (or sign up if you're new).

2\. Click on "Add Website" in the left sidebar.

3\. Choose your plan:

\- Select either Pro or Enterprise subscription

\- Choose between monthly or annual billing

4\. Review your order and enter payment details:

\- Confirm the plan and pricing

\- Enter your credit card information or select a saved payment method

5\. Click "Subscribe" to complete your purchase.

6\. You'll be directed to the snippet installation page:

\- Copy the provided tracking snippet

\- Install it on your website (typically just before the closing </head> tag)

7\. Verify your installation:

\- Click the "Verify Installation" button

\- We'll check if the snippet is correctly installed

8\. Start exploring your heatmaps!

Remember:

\- If you're tracking e-commerce data, don't forget to install the revenue snippet as well.

\- For platform-specific installation guides (e.g., Shopify, WordPress), check our documentation.

Need help? Our support team is available via chat or at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

# Notification Email Summaries | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/13392341-notification-email-summaries#main-content)

Notification Email Summaries
============================

January 14, 2026

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/13392341-notification-email-summaries#h_1ea982a2e9)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/13392341-notification-email-summaries#h_6fde7bc229)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/13392341-notification-email-summaries#h_aa601cf962)

Notification Email Summaries are AI-powered performance alerts delivered to your inbox at the frequency you choose! These summaries highlight key trends in your site performance and are designed to help you quickly identify what’s working and what needs attention right in your inbox.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1941507137/29b8e7767d823cf79a2544dfc1c3/CleanShot+2026-01-06+at+4%E2%80%AF_36_38%402x.png?expires=1789486200&signature=b9f3a8ecade6defc0fed919e8df3b7cb6b288deb80c48e781fe307d6f826334f&req=dSkjF8x%2BmoBcXvMW1HO4zUesVO7CqulXuW9RP1A8xWZLMqyNrFnQkF06GLjI%0AqHpakveRxxQnyWniN9E%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1941507137/29b8e7767d823cf79a2544dfc1c3/CleanShot+2026-01-06+at+4%E2%80%AF_36_38%402x.png?expires=1789486200&signature=b9f3a8ecade6defc0fed919e8df3b7cb6b288deb80c48e781fe307d6f826334f&req=dSkjF8x%2BmoBcXvMW1HO4zUesVO7CqulXuW9RP1A8xWZLMqyNrFnQkF06GLjI%0AqHpakveRxxQnyWniN9E%3D%0A)

What’s Included
---------------

Each email contains a 7-day performance comparison across six key metrics and a high-level AI Insight:

*   Engaged Sessions
    
*   Website Revenue
    
*   Website CVR
    
*   Revenue per Session
    
*   Website AOV
    
*   Page Views
    
*   High-Level AI Performance Insight
    

You'll be able to review current trends to ensure that you're always in the loop.

For more information on Heatmap's Data Definitions & Methodology, reference our article [here](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/11510254-heatmap-data-definitions-methodology)
.

How to Manage Your Email Settings
---------------------------------

You can manage your Email Summary preferences during Onboarding or in your Heatmap Settings. To find this, you can go to Settings > Notifications > Performance Summaries and/or Critical Drop Alerts.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1941543119/5a85d94b6ca0438efa6284190907/Screenshot+2026-01-14+at+2_19_34%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1789486200&signature=2bfc1d303f1fa0b91056b88a1f21cbec957ce877a39a49ab7677118dc30693f8&req=dSkjF8x6noBeUPMW1HO4zdrnLajfVAPOveyXHtkjhUJya8M3BNPsIKWFNAOp%0Aj6UQx7%2Fs0LU4W%2F7zcoc%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1941543119/5a85d94b6ca0438efa6284190907/Screenshot+2026-01-14+at+2_19_34%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1789486200&signature=2bfc1d303f1fa0b91056b88a1f21cbec957ce877a39a49ab7677118dc30693f8&req=dSkjF8x6noBeUPMW1HO4zdrnLajfVAPOveyXHtkjhUJya8M3BNPsIKWFNAOp%0Aj6UQx7%2Fs0LU4W%2F7zcoc%3D%0A)

### Performance Summaries

Performance Summaries will allow you to receive an email summary of your metrics.

Here you'll have the option to choose the following:

*   Delivery Frequency (Weekly, Biweekly, Monthly)
    
*   Day of Week
    
*   Email Address
    
*   Connect via Slack
    
*   Ability to turn these on or off
    

### Critical Drop Alerts

Critical Drop Alerts are proactive emails sent to your inbox to ensure whether any selected metrics drop dramatically.

Here you'll have the option to choose the following:

*   Monitored Key Metrics (Engaged Sessions, Conversion Rate, Website AOV, Website Revenue, Revenue Per Session, Page Views)
    
*   Email Address
    
*   Connect via Slack
    
*   Ability to turn these on or off

Have a question or need a hand? Our team is here to help. Reach out anytime via chat, [schedule an onboarding call](https://meetings.hubspot.com/heatmap/support)
, or email us at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)

Heatmap Data Table
==================

Data Table

Updated this week

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_429d6a7dd9)

The Data Table feature in Heatmap.com provides detailed, quantitative insights into your webpage elements' performance. This powerful tool complements your visual heatmaps with precise metrics, allowing for in-depth analysis of user interactions and conversions.

**Table of Contents:**

*   **[Accessing the Data Table](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_d22147721d)
    **
    
*   **[Key Features and Functions](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_e7cf57fb2c)
    **
    
*   **[Best Practices for Using the Data Table](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_19bef75c88)
    **
    
*   **[AI Naming in Heatmap.com](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_fc3b590354)
    **
    
*   **[Customizing AI-Generated Names](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_0791873500)
    **
    
*   **[Understanding Full Page Metrics in Data Tables](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_c9cf1fe0ee)
    **
    
*   **[How to Export Data Table Analytics](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508420-heatmap-data-table#h_4f8b40a221)
    **
    

* * *

### **Accessing the Data Table**

1\. Log into your Heatmap.com account

2\. Navigate to your desired heatmap page

3\. Click the "Data Table" button located at the top of the page to expand the feature

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652131419/63a308ee501086206edc79c2ecdb/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=61753c3dba150a50c74fbfc63d55c6114df73da5b94d2c66ba856e00e7818e0b&req=dSYiFMh9nIVeUPMW1HO4zTSqe7w9S77p4j7li6y8gUPC7uo3CJMjtPcELHqT%0A6d7mkV9MX7INpqbOWVQ%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652131419/63a308ee501086206edc79c2ecdb/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=61753c3dba150a50c74fbfc63d55c6114df73da5b94d2c66ba856e00e7818e0b&req=dSYiFMh9nIVeUPMW1HO4zTSqe7w9S77p4j7li6y8gUPC7uo3CJMjtPcELHqT%0A6d7mkV9MX7INpqbOWVQ%3D%0A)

* * *

### **Key Features and Functions**

**1\. Search Functionality**  
​Use the search bar at the top of the table to quickly find specific elements by name

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652132260/bd1dd1079d1edb556960e16f94f3/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=dc01ac4f9b178a6bba59c81e1c8bb2f608e9f33a2162d248a2c92afab6579130&req=dSYiFMh9n4NZWfMW1HO4zZ7nByvEOS4G8Ig7IyW3Ospc9T4HXmaVMHP6pXqs%0Ar137aIlMwS0VPo5cY7M%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652132260/bd1dd1079d1edb556960e16f94f3/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=dc01ac4f9b178a6bba59c81e1c8bb2f608e9f33a2162d248a2c92afab6579130&req=dSYiFMh9n4NZWfMW1HO4zZ7nByvEOS4G8Ig7IyW3Ospc9T4HXmaVMHP6pXqs%0Ar137aIlMwS0VPo5cY7M%3D%0A)

**2\. Comprehensive Metrics**

View detailed data for each page element, including:

*   Clicks
    
*   Purchases
    
*   Revenue
    
*   Conversion Rate (eCVR)
    
*   Average Order Value (AOV)
    
*   Revenue Per Click (RPC)
    
*   Revenue Per Session (RPS)
    
*   Scroll % (what % of customers see each element)
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652133392/36ddcee35c0eaccea74355d75fc2/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=f753fd417dae4bce5ac8619ca1b14f376da2d55492a8f480993c553a184027c9&req=dSYiFMh9noJWW%2FMW1HO4zQYPIiux95329YXjypfARwWcLXRvSbahoLoAQIQC%0AdzN%2Fh0o95CniIx9GPFI%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652133392/36ddcee35c0eaccea74355d75fc2/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=f753fd417dae4bce5ac8619ca1b14f376da2d55492a8f480993c553a184027c9&req=dSYiFMh9noJWW%2FMW1HO4zQYPIiux95329YXjypfARwWcLXRvSbahoLoAQIQC%0AdzN%2Fh0o95CniIx9GPFI%3D%0A)

**3\. Full Page Metrics**  
​The first row of the table shows aggregated data for the entire page, providing a quick overview of overall performance.

**Note:** this is a combination of all elements so it will show higher numbers than “total page revenue.” This makes it easier to analyze page-by-page metrics vs sitewide metrics.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652134659/a784603c776895c1d730c440a353/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=05d8e0867b1d1692233eafac58bd03fb3c9df66cce8a680b88d99f84dac5b0e5&req=dSYiFMh9mYdaUPMW1HO4ze%2F38K3TzP9t1U7yGkBB1Hru7TxHWSFm5WzU8NXh%0A3syIBUo7FF24%2BRgyE0s%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652134659/a784603c776895c1d730c440a353/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=05d8e0867b1d1692233eafac58bd03fb3c9df66cce8a680b88d99f84dac5b0e5&req=dSYiFMh9mYdaUPMW1HO4ze%2F38K3TzP9t1U7yGkBB1Hru7TxHWSFm5WzU8NXh%0A3syIBUo7FF24%2BRgyE0s%3D%0A)

**4\. Interactive Element Highlighting**

Click on any row in the table to highlight the corresponding element on your heatmap

A modal will appear with detailed data for the selected element

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652136131/2c138299dae2110ff63eab786ac4/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=a7b5532fa0579e7de8284610586904c8b08c4f908d3a8c57578451640bfcf1a6&req=dSYiFMh9m4BcWPMW1HO4zTZ8sl4pTYTAvIveGMfxG%2BXXUzALfQ3JXyJ0S1%2Bi%0A6p2I9m0lKLRhHaBtPXM%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652136131/2c138299dae2110ff63eab786ac4/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=a7b5532fa0579e7de8284610586904c8b08c4f908d3a8c57578451640bfcf1a6&req=dSYiFMh9m4BcWPMW1HO4zTZ8sl4pTYTAvIveGMfxG%2BXXUzALfQ3JXyJ0S1%2Bi%0A6p2I9m0lKLRhHaBtPXM%3D%0A)

**5\. Customization Options**  
​Resize the data table by dragging its edges to fit your viewing preferences

**6\. Data Export**  
​Use the export button in the top right corner to download your data for further analysis or reporting

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652138480/12d7b9065112dc810c4c32469f1d/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=1dfd6d73f3f5cfd4cebdfa10d7ef2344c047c2045d7a7d1f0748f5b287d4bbca&req=dSYiFMh9lYVXWfMW1HO4zcv%2F%2FH3qPxFP1SrjrsfcD6o9UrGNQNUQHFVdTenv%0Ade9cky3CFgDOo50LnJQ%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652138480/12d7b9065112dc810c4c32469f1d/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=1dfd6d73f3f5cfd4cebdfa10d7ef2344c047c2045d7a7d1f0748f5b287d4bbca&req=dSYiFMh9lYVXWfMW1HO4zcv%2F%2FH3qPxFP1SrjrsfcD6o9UrGNQNUQHFVdTenv%0Ade9cky3CFgDOo50LnJQ%3D%0A)

**7\. Comparison Mode Compatibility**  
​The data table works seamlessly with comparison mode, allowing you to analyze metrics across different segments or time periods

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652140383/c179315ad60f983344a9791e9a65/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=54d72d0ef748615fd6272b9e806036556aba7d97ad970cdd7d8d3e8defdc3fbf&req=dSYiFMh6nYJXWvMW1HO4zaLXxWfDL0MMPvt%2FsY0IEkbJXqhdG8Wen4cJOeKg%0AzotQIrssJy065ktfVQI%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652140383/c179315ad60f983344a9791e9a65/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=54d72d0ef748615fd6272b9e806036556aba7d97ad970cdd7d8d3e8defdc3fbf&req=dSYiFMh6nYJXWvMW1HO4zaLXxWfDL0MMPvt%2FsY0IEkbJXqhdG8Wen4cJOeKg%0AzotQIrssJy065ktfVQI%3D%0A)

* * *

### **Best Practices for Using the Data Table**  

1\. Start with **Full Page Metrics** to understand overall page performance

2\. Use the _Search_ function to focus on specific elements of interest

3\. Compare metrics between different elements to identify top performers and areas for improvement

4\. Regularly export data to track changes over time or share insights with your team

5\. Use in conjunction with visual heatmaps for a complete understanding of user behavior

The Data Table feature provides a powerful, data-driven complement to your visual heatmaps, offering a comprehensive view of your page's performance and user interactions.

* * *

### **AI Naming in Heatmap.com**

AI naming is a powerful feature in Heatmap.com that automatically identifies and labels key elements on your website. This article explains how it works and how to use it effectively.

### **What is AI Naming?**

AI naming uses a custom-built machine learning algorithm to analyze your website's structure and content and automatically assigns proper names to important elements like buttons, search bars, product tiles, and many others.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652143297/de2f772174f5d94c6d1175e17a9f/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=8e540a750df4585d3fa2cc6e58f7498f71d50093431c547d68d04f3c133fcd5e&req=dSYiFMh6noNWXvMW1HO4za8k23%2BJiT2YI3M9zvO2xV8hgo4v%2B0AG2PObXRTy%0AAuQPyYAaql1WPhwxnH8%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652143297/de2f772174f5d94c6d1175e17a9f/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=8e540a750df4585d3fa2cc6e58f7498f71d50093431c547d68d04f3c133fcd5e&req=dSYiFMh6noNWXvMW1HO4za8k23%2BJiT2YI3M9zvO2xV8hgo4v%2B0AG2PObXRTy%0AAuQPyYAaql1WPhwxnH8%3D%0A)

### **Benefits of AI Naming**

*   Saves time by eliminating manual labeling
    
*   Ensures consistent naming across your site
    
*   Improves accuracy of heatmap and user behavior analysis
    

### **Best Practices for Accurate AI Naming**

To ensure the most accurate AI naming results:

*   Use standard best practices when building your website.
    
*   Implement proper naming conventions for your HTML elements.
    
*   Use appropriate HTML tags and elements for their intended purposes.
    
*   Provide descriptive IDs and classes for important elements.
    

Following these practices will significantly improve the AI's ability to correctly identify and name elements on your site.

### **Customizing AI-Generated Names**

Customizing element names in your data table helps you organize and analyze your heatmap data more effectively.

While AI naming is generally accurate, you can always adjust names if needed.

* * *

### **Here are the steps to update the element names:**

1\. Open Your Heatmap: Navigate to the heatmap page you want to modify.

2\. Access the Data Table: Click on the "Data Table" button to view detailed analytics.

3\. Locate the Element: Find the row containing the element you want to rename.

4\. Click the Name Field: In the "Name" column, click on the current name of the element.

5\. Edit the Name: A text input field will appear. Type in your desired new name.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652144553/a44d632a39907d1cd4a4e8215654/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=3de57a24cc761f8569d4521e06b5f8967dcb41dcf9d5c5bee7515ae1c40cbc53&req=dSYiFMh6mYRaWvMW1HO4zRuZ1w5k6kyBq3n5ECC6AmMB0JEFvYeBxYXB8%2F%2B%2F%0AFMTiIlB6U5oZBuWzsck%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652144553/a44d632a39907d1cd4a4e8215654/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=3de57a24cc761f8569d4521e06b5f8967dcb41dcf9d5c5bee7515ae1c40cbc53&req=dSYiFMh6mYRaWvMW1HO4zRuZ1w5k6kyBq3n5ECC6AmMB0JEFvYeBxYXB8%2F%2B%2F%0AFMTiIlB6U5oZBuWzsck%3D%0A)

6\. Save Changes: Press Enter or click outside the field to save the new name.

7\. Verify the Update: The data table will refresh, displaying the updated name.

**Remember:**

*   Choose clear, descriptive names for easy identification
    
*   Renamed elements will retain their new names in future sessions
    
*   Changes only affect your view and do not alter the website's actual HTML
    

**Customizing names can help you:**

*   Group similar elements together
    
*   Identify specific areas of interest more quickly
    
*   Create more meaningful reports
    

By renaming elements in your data table, you can tailor your heatmap analysis to your specific needs and make insights more accessible to your team.

* * *

### **Understanding Full Page Metrics in Data Tables**

Full Page Metrics provide a comprehensive overview of your entire webpage's performance in Heatmap.com's data tables. This feature allows you to quickly assess overall user engagement and conversion metrics for the page you're analyzing.

**What are Full Page Metrics?**

Full Page Metrics aggregate data from all tracked elements on your webpage, giving you a bird's-eye view of page performance. These metrics appear as a special row at the top of your data table.

**Where to Find Full Page Metrics**

1\. Open any heatmap in your Heatmap.com dashboard.

2\. Click on the "Data Table" button to expand the data view.

3\. The Full Page Metrics row is always the first entry in your data table, labeled as "Full Page Metrics."

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652146370/f8663360b78bceaca4f77ffc09fb/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=57b475501d4ac28238cb5fbd139341f27da8d2147452ebb689e981a3bfb96d34&req=dSYiFMh6m4JYWfMW1HO4zUOZZoQkZhEhIEPlUxtJTKWNOO%2Fy5%2B1xsUwrSVJI%0AdMkFNTVCXhvO%2FwRPze0%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1652146370/f8663360b78bceaca4f77ffc09fb/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=57b475501d4ac28238cb5fbd139341f27da8d2147452ebb689e981a3bfb96d34&req=dSYiFMh6m4JYWfMW1HO4zUOZZoQkZhEhIEPlUxtJTKWNOO%2Fy5%2B1xsUwrSVJI%0AdMkFNTVCXhvO%2FwRPze0%3D%0A)

**Metrics Included**

Full Page Metrics typically include:

*   Total Clicks
    
*   Total Purchases
    
*   Total Revenue
    
*   Total Conversion Rate (eCVR)
    
*   Total Average Order Value (AOV)
    
*   Total Revenue Per Click (RPC)
    
*   Total Revenue Per Session (RPS)
    
*   Total Scroll % (what % of customers see each element)
    

* * *

### **How to Use Full Page Metrics**

*   Use these metrics as a baseline to compare individual element performance.
    
*   Track overall page performance over time.
    
*   Quickly assess the impact of page-wide changes or A/B tests.
    

**Best Practices**

*   Regularly review Full Page Metrics to understand overall page health.
    
*   Compare Full Page Metrics across different pages to identify top-performing and underperforming pages.
    
*   Use these metrics in conjunction with individual element data for a complete understanding of page performance.
    

* * *

Heatmap.com offers a straightforward and efficient method for exporting your data table information.

This feature allows you to analyze your data offline, create custom reports, or share insights with your team. Here's a comprehensive guide to the export option available:

**1\. Accessing the Export Feature**

# Understanding and Using IP Blocking | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023965-understanding-and-using-ip-blocking#main-content)

Understanding and Using IP Blocking
===================================

IP Blocking, data accuracy, exclude team, customer behavior, heatmap analytics, IP address, IPv4, manual IP entry, cleaner data, agency-friendly, heatmap dashboard, analytics

October 21, 2024

**Understanding and Using IP Blocking**

IP Blocking is a powerful feature that helps increase the accuracy of your analytics data by excluding specific users, such as your team members, from being tracked. This guide will explain what IP Blocking is, why it's important, and how to use it effectively.

**What is IP Blocking?**

IP Blocking allows you to exclude specific IP addresses from your heatmap analytics. This means that visits from these IP addresses won't be recorded or included in your data, giving you a more accurate picture of your actual customer behavior.

**Why Use IP Blocking?**

1\. Improved Data Accuracy: By excluding your team members' frequent visits, you get a clearer view of genuine customer interactions.

2\. One-Time Setup: Once configured, IP Blocking works automatically for all future sessions.

3\. Agency-Friendly: Agencies can set this up once to exclude their team from all current and future client analytics.

**How IP Blocking Works**

Every device connected to the internet has an IP address. For IP Blocking, we use the IPv4 address. When a visit comes from a blocked IP, our system simply doesn't record that session in your analytics.

**Setting Up IP Blocking**

1\. Log in to your heatmap dashboard

2\. Navigate to the IP Blocking section

3\. You have two options:

a. Click "Use my IP" to automatically add your current IP address

b. Manually enter an IPv4 address (you can find this at whatismyip.com)

4\. Give the IP a name (e.g., "Office Network")

5\. Click "Save"

That's it! Two clicks, and you're done.

**Why IP Blocking Matters**

Think about how often you and your team visit your website. All of these visits are currently included in your analytics, potentially skewing your data. By implementing IP Blocking, you ensure that your heatmap data reflects genuine customer behavior, allowing you to make better, more informed decisions about your website's performance and user experience.

**Best Practices**

\- Block IPs for all office locations and remote workers

\- For agencies, set this up for each client to ensure clean data across all projects

\- Regularly review and update your blocked IPs, especially if your team changes locations or grows

**Need Help?**

If you're unsure about which IPs to block or need assistance setting up IP Blocking, our support team is here to help. We're committed to ensuring you get the most accurate and valuable insights from your heatmap data.

Remember, cleaner data leads to better decisions. Start using IP Blocking today to refine your analytics and unlock more accurate insights into your customer behavior!

**General Questions**
=====================

**What is Heatmap Funnels?**
----------------------------

Heatmap Funnels is a comprehensive tool that helps you visualize and analyze the customer journey through your website. It lets you track how users navigate different steps through the customer journey and identifies where users drop off, to help you optimize your conversion paths.

In Heatmap Funnels, you can build step-by-step breakdowns, including specific pages and events, to explore various journey paths to make the best data-driven decisions.  
​

  
**How does Heatmap Funnels benefit my business?**
----------------------------------------------------

The system provides valuable insights into user behavior, allowing you to:

*   Identify friction points in your conversion process
    
*   Understand which pages or events contribute to successful conversions
    
*   Compare performance across different devices and time periods
    
*   Make data-driven decisions to improve your conversion rates
    

  
**When should I use Heatmap Funnels?**
-----------------------------------------

Use Heatmap Funnels to map and optimize conversion rates by examining the entire customer journey, from discovery to purchase and every step in between.

A funnel will visually show how your website users progress through each step, and where they drop off.

Here are a few reasons _when_ to use Heatmap Funnels:

*   If your business is in a conversion slump, funnels are a great way to run a diagnostic check to discover where users are dropping in the customer journey.
    
*   If you run multiple ad campaigns, ensure your landing page is effective and the user completes every step of the journey. This will help prevent wasted ad spend.
    
*   If you're launching a new product, you need to understand the performance of your existing product. Create a product funnel to find the performance of a specific product and discover where you can A/B test or improve UI and UX for the customer for your next launch.
    
*   Landing page funnels are excellent if you run email campaigns. Landing page funnels will help you discover real-time data on their performance. You can see if the landing page and email resonate with your customers who click through.
    

*   Planning a website relaunch? Discover where to optimize your website for a high conversion rate.
    
*   Cart abandonment funnels target high-intent users just one or two steps away from converting into customers. These funnels can help you optimize recovery strategies, such as retargeting ads, email campaigns, and personalized offers.
    

* * *

**Working with Funnels**
========================

**What types of funnels are available?**
----------------------------------------

There are two main categories of funnels:

1.  **Pre-built funnels** - Ready-to-use analytics funnels like purchase cart abandonment and purchase journey
    
2.  **Custom funnels** - Funnels you create based on your specific business needs
    

  
**What's the difference between pre-built and custom funnels?**
------------------------------------------------------------------

Pre-built funnels are designed for common e-commerce journeys and have limited editing capabilities (only the date range can be modified). Custom funnels provide full flexibility in defining steps and conditions, and they can be fully edited or deleted as needed.

  

---

* * *

  
**Funnel Configuration**
===========================

**How do I create a funnel?**
-----------------------------

1.  Navigate to the **Funnels** section in your Heatmap dashboard
    
2.  Click “**Build New Funnel.**”
    
3.  Add a title to your funnel. This will help you stay organized while building multiple funnels in Heatmap.
    
4.  Add your first step by clicking “**Choose a condition**” and selecting from specific pages or events. Funnels are built by selecting specific pages and events that represent steps in your customer journey.
    
5.  Once you’ve completed populating the condition, click “**Add Step**” to build the next step in the funnel. Continue adding additional steps until you reach the end goal.
    
6.  Once you’re done, click “**Save Funnel**” to save the funnel.
    

**How many funnels can I create?**
----------------------------------

There is no limit to how many funnels you can create. Once you generate your funnels, your data allows you to analyze the data from them to make data-driven decisions about your CRO strategies.  
​

**What types of steps can I add to my funnel?**
-----------------------------------------------

You can add various step types, including:

*   All Sessions (starting point)
    
*   Page visits (specific URLs, PDPs, collection pages)
    
*   Events (add to cart, checkout, purchases)
    

**Are there any rules for creating funnel steps?**
--------------------------------------------------

Yes, there are several logical rules to ensure proper funnel construction:

*   "All Sessions" can only be used as the first step
    
*   Once an event is selected, only events can be used in subsequent steps
    
*   Pages can be reordered and duplicated
    
*   Events cannot be reordered or duplicated
    

**How many steps can I add to a custom funnel?**
------------------------------------------------

You can add multiple steps to create a comprehensive funnel that accurately represents your user journey. While there's no strict limit, we recommend keeping funnels focused with 3-7 steps for optimal analysis.  
​

**Can I edit pre-built funnels?**
---------------------------------

Pre-built funnels are static and have limited editing capabilities. You can modify the date range and add filters for a more tailored analysis, but the steps and structure cannot be changed. This ensures consistent analysis for standard journeys. If you want to create a more custom funnel, click "Build a New Funnel" in the Funnels tab.  
​

**Why can't I delete pre-built funnels?**
-----------------------------------------

Pre-built funnels are designed as standard analytics tools that provide consistent insights for common journeys. Since they're integral to the platform's analytics suite, they cannot be deleted.  
​

**Why is the "Build New Funnel" button greyed out?**
----------------------------------------------------

If there's a data configuration issue with no data flowing in, or if you're editing a funnel but haven't saved it yet, the "Build New Funnel" button may be greyed out. If you're still experiencing issues, please reach out to customer support.

* * *

  
**Analysis and Filtering**
=============================

**What filtering options are available for funnels?**
-----------------------------------------------------

You can filter your funnel data by:

*   Date range (custom periods or preset options)
    
*   Device types (desktop, mobile, tablet)
    
*   Standard filters consistent with other platform tools
    

**Can I see how different devices affect my funnel performance?**
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Yes, the device type filter allows you to analyze and compare funnel performance across desktop, mobile, and tablet users, helping you identify device-specific optimization opportunities.  
​

**Does the system support regex for URL matching?**
---------------------------------------------------

Regex support for URL matching will be available in an upcoming update, enabling more advanced pattern matching for page-based funnel steps.  
​

**How accurate is the funnel data?**
------------------------------------

The funnel data undergoes comprehensive quality assurance testing to ensure accuracy. Our system tracks human user sessions and events in real-time, providing reliable insights for your analysis. We do not track the robots.  
​

**How is the completed percentage calculated?**
-----------------------------------------------

The completed percentage at each step of your funnel shows how many users took the specified action from one step to the next. This is calculated by the number of users who took the specified action divided by the number of completed users in the previous step, not from the start of the funnel.

**How is the abandoned percentage calculated?**
-----------------------------------------------

The abandoned percentage at each funnel stage shows how many users did not take the specified action and dropped out of the funnel before reaching the next step. This highlights the “loss” of users within your designated funnel. The abandoned percentage is calculated by the number of users who did not take the specified action divided by the number of completed users in the previous step, not from the start of the funnel. This abandoned percentage is where you can identify user friction points within the journey.

**How is drop-off calculated between steps?**
---------------------------------------------

Drop-off in your funnel is calculated based on the number of users who do not take a specified action from one step to the next. This will be noted as the abandoned users for each respective step.

Both the completed users and abandoned users for each respective step are equivalent to all completed users in the step prior. As steps progress through the funnel, the number of users will narrow down, highlighting the user segment completing all actions within the funnel.

Every funnel is expected to have a natural drop-off. You should never anticipate the user total increasing as additional steps are added to the funnel.

**How do I interpret funnel drop-off?**
---------------------------------------

Interpreting funnel drop-off is about understanding where users abandon the journey as they move through your site and why, so you can take action to improve conversions. Large abandoned user percentages highlight key drop-off points within the funnel, noting for you to further review specific parts of the journey.

For example, if there is a significant funnel drop-off between Add to Cart and Checkout, this could signal that customers are having a friction point with unexpected shipping costs, have a lack of trust, or need a sense of urgency in your product.

Using features like heatmaps and screen recordings can help provide a deeper understanding of why users are dropping off and specific optimizations to make. Just be sure to review the steps prior to a large drop-off to understand why abandoned users didn’t take the specified action.  
​

* * *

**Troubleshooting**
===================

**Who do I contact if I have additional questions?**
----------------------------------------------------

For additional support with Heatmap Funnels, please contact our customer support team through the help center or by emailing [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

# How Long Does It Take for Heatmap Data to Appear? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023997-how-long-does-it-take-for-heatmap-data-to-appear#main-content)

How Long Does It Take for Heatmap Data to Appear?
=================================================

Heatmap data timing, site structure visibility, initial data,traffic accumulation, continuous updates, site traffic, page popularity

October 21, 2024

Thank you for choosing Heatmap.com! We understand you're eager to see your site's heatmap data. Here's what you can expect regarding the timing of data appearance:

1\. Immediate Site Structure Visibility

As soon as you integrate Heatmap.com:

• All pages on your site will be visible in the left side-panel.

• You can click on any page to view its heatmap, even without traffic data.

• This gives you an instant overview of your site's structure.

2\. Data Appearance Timeline

• Initial Data: Basic heatmap data typically appears within hours for pages receiving traffic.

• Full Data: Most sites see comprehensive data within 24 hours.

• Maximum Wait: In rare cases, it may take up to 48 hours for full data to appear.

3\. Continuous Updates

• Our system automatically refreshes data every few hours.

• Heatmaps become more detailed over time as more user interactions are recorded.

4\. Factors Affecting Data Accumulation

• Site Traffic: Higher-traffic sites generally accumulate data faster.

• Page Popularity: Frequently visited pages will show more detailed heatmaps sooner.

5\. Data Reliability for Analysis

• Basic Analysis: Can typically begin within a day for most sites.

• Detailed Analysis: For advanced features like Revenue Per Click, we recommend at least 5,000 to 7,000 mobile sessions for reliable insights.

6\. Monitoring Progress

• Regularly check your dashboard to see data accumulation.

• Use the date range selector to track progress over time.

If you don't see any data after 48 hours on pages you know have received traffic, please contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 for assistance.

Remember: While you can immediately see your site structure, the richness and accuracy of heatmap data improves over time as more visitor interactions are recorded. Patience during the initial data collection period will result in more valuable insights for your website optimization efforts.

# How long does it take for JavaScript error fixes to update on the dashboard? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023990-how-long-does-it-take-for-javascript-error-fixes-to-update-on-the-dashboard#main-content)

How long does it take for JavaScript error fixes to update on the dashboard?
============================================================================

JavaScript error fixes, dashboard updates, update schedule, browser cache, ongoing monitoring, Heatmap.com, error reoccurrence

October 21, 2024

**How long does it take for JavaScript error fixes to update on the dashboard?**

If you've recently fixed JavaScript errors on your website, you may be wondering when these changes will be reflected on your heatmap dashboard. Here's what you need to know:

**Dashboard Update Schedule**

Our system has a process that runs every few hours to update the data on your dashboard. This means that once you've fixed JavaScript errors on your site, you should see these changes reflected in your dashboard within the next update cycle.

**Typical Timeframe**

In most cases, you can expect to see updates to your JavaScript error status within 2-6 hours after implementing fixes. However, the exact timing can vary depending on when you made the changes relative to our update schedule.

**What to Expect**

\- If you've successfully fixed all JavaScript errors, they should disappear from your dashboard in the next update cycle.

\- New data collected after your fixes will not include these resolved errors.

\- Historical data from before the fix will still show previous errors.

**If You Don't See Updates**

If it's been more than 6 hours since you fixed the errors and you're still seeing them on your dashboard:

1\. Verify that the fixes were successfully deployed to your live site.

2\. Check if the errors are still occurring using browser developer tools.

3\. Clear your browser cache and reload the dashboard to ensure you're seeing the most recent data.

**Ongoing Monitoring**

Remember that JavaScript errors can sometimes reoccur due to changes in your website or third-party scripts. We recommend regularly checking your dashboard to ensure your site remains error-free.

By utilizing our regular update cycles, you can be confident that your dashboard will accurately reflect the current state of your website's JavaScript performance. If you have any questions or concerns about JavaScript errors or dashboard updates, don't hesitate to reach out to our support team for assistance.

# How Heatmap.com Works | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10023974-how-heatmap-com-works#main-content)

How Heatmap.com Works
=====================

client-side tracking, real-time data, user behavior, JavaScript snippet, heatmaps, click maps, scroll maps, data anonymization, IP blocking, Heatmap.com, insights

October 21, 2024

Heatmap utilizes advanced client-side tracking technology to provide you with comprehensive insights into user behavior on your website. This document explains the core mechanisms behind our tracking system and how we transform raw data into actionable insights.

**Client-Side Tracking Basics**

Heatmap's tracking system operates primarily on the client side, meaning it runs directly in the user's browser. This approach offers several advantages:

*   Real-time data collection
    
*   Minimal impact on server load
    
*   Ability to capture detailed user interactions
    

**Data Collection Process**

**2.1 Tracking Snippet Installation**

The process begins when you install our lightweight JavaScript tracking snippet in your website's <head> section. This snippet serves as the foundation for all data collection.

**2.2 User Interaction Capture**

Once installed, the snippet monitors various user interactions, including:

*   Mouse movements
    
*   Clicks
    
*   Scrolling behavior
    
*   Time spent on page
    
*   Device and browser information
    

**2.3 Revenue Data Collection**

Our unique revenue tracking snippet (Heatmap Pixel) captures transaction data, allowing us to correlate user behavior with actual revenue generation.

**Data Processing and Visualization**

**3.1 Data Transmission**

Collected data is securely transmitted to our servers in real-time or at regular intervals, depending on the interaction type.

**3.2 Data Aggregation**

Our servers aggregate the received data, combining information from multiple users to create comprehensive behavior profiles.

**3.3 Heatmap Generation**

The aggregated data is then used to generate various types of heatmaps:

Click maps: Visualizing where users click most frequently

Scroll maps: Showing how far users scroll down pages

Move maps: Illustrating cursor movement patterns

**3.4 AI-Powered Analysis**

Our heatmapAI system analyzes the collected data, identifying patterns and generating actionable insights.

**Privacy and Security**

**4.1 Data Anonymization**

All collected data is anonymized to protect user privacy. We do not track or store personally identifiable information.

**4.2 Secure Transmission**

Data is transmitted using industry-standard encryption protocols to ensure security.

**4.3 IP Blocking**

Our system allows for IP blocking to exclude internal traffic, ensuring your data accurately reflects genuine user behavior.

**Performance Considerations**

**5.1 Asynchronous Loading**

Our tracking script loads asynchronously, minimizing impact on your website's load time.

**5.2 Efficient Data Handling**

We employ efficient data handling techniques to ensure minimal CPU and memory usage on the client side.

**5.3 Content Delivery Network (CDN)**

Our scripts are delivered via a global CDN, ensuring fast loading times regardless of user location.

**Advanced Features**

**6.1 JavaScript Error Tracking**

In addition to user behavior, our system can track JavaScript errors on your site, helping you identify and resolve technical issues that may impact user experience.

**6.2 Site Speed Monitoring**

We continuously monitor your site's speed, allowing you to correlate performance metrics with user behavior and conversion rates.

**6.3 Custom Event Tracking**

For more complex websites, we offer the ability to track custom events, giving you insights into specific user actions unique to your site.

**Conclusion**

Heatmap's client-side tracking technology offers a powerful, non-intrusive way to gain deep insights into user behavior on your website. By combining sophisticated data collection methods with advanced analysis and visualization techniques, we provide you with the tools you need to optimize your site's performance and user experience.

For more detailed information on specific features or for technical support, please don't hesitate to contact our support team.

Can Heatmaps Capture Cart and Checkout Pages?
=============================================

cart and checkout tracking, Heatmap privacy, sensitive data, security, data protection, sales funnel optimization, cart abandonment analysis, compliance

October 21, 2024

**Can Heatmaps Capture Cart and Checkout Pages?**

No, Heatmap does not capture data from cart and checkout pages. This is a deliberate choice to protect user privacy and ensure the security of sensitive information.

**Why We Don't Track These Pages:**

1\. Privacy Protection: Cart and checkout pages often contain personal and financial information.

2\. Security: Excluding these pages helps prevent any potential exposure of sensitive data.

3\. Compliance: This approach aligns with various data protection regulations.

**What You Can Do Instead:**

\- Focus on optimizing other parts of your sales funnel using Heatmap data.

\- Use alternative, secure methods to analyze cart abandonment and checkout completion rates.

If you have any questions about our data collection practices or need advice on optimizing your e-commerce process, please contact our support team.

HeatmapAI is an AI-powered feature built into Heatmap that delivers weekly recommendations and insights to help improve your website’s performance. It combines your site’s behavioral and revenue data with industry best practices to generate clear, actionable suggestions.

The goal of HeatmapAI is to help you optimize for Revenue Per Session (RPS) by improving user experience, page performance, and conversion opportunities.

HeatmapAI Features
==================

HeatmapAI is beneficial because it transforms complex user behavior and performance data into clear, actionable recommendations that help you improve conversions and maximize revenue.

Dashboard Overview
------------------

Every week, HeatmapAI provides a high-level performance update comparing your current period of data to the previous period.

*   **Weekly Performance Insight** \- A snapshot of how your site is trending period over period.

Heatmaps
--------

Within each Heatmap page, HeatmapAi delivers 10 AI-powered insights per page every week.

*   Recommendations draw from all user interaction (ie: clicks, scrolls, purchases, etc.)
    
*   Suggestions are tied to CRO best practices
    
*   Insights mainly highlight what can be improved and most impactful

Surveys
-------

HeatmapAI reviews open-ended survey responses and provides a summary of customer feedback to give you clear answers.

*   Surfaces sentiment and recurring issues or opportunities
    
*   Reduces the need to manually sift through individual responses

Quickly understand what customers are saying at scale, so you can prioritize improvements.

How HeatmapAI Works
===================

*   **Data-Driven:** Recommendations are based on trillions of user interactions and over 1,000 websites, plus your own site's behavior and revenue data
    
*   **Tailored to Your Site:** Every suggestion takes your specific audience and business model into account
    
*   **Focused on RPS:** Unlike generic conversion metrics, HeatmapAI prioritizes Revenue per Session, combining conversion rate and average order value for a clearer picture of performance

# Why Is a Section of My Page Not Visible in the Heatmap? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024082-why-is-a-section-of-my-page-not-visible-in-the-heatmap#main-content)

Why Is a Section of My Page Not Visible in the Heatmap?
=======================================================

dynamic content, lazy loading, iframe content, pop-ups, overlays, recent page changes, scrolling issues, JavaScript conflicts

October 21, 2024

**Why Is a Section of My Page Not Visible in the Heatmap?**

If you've noticed that a section of your webpage is missing or not visible in your heatmap, don't worry. This is a common issue that can occur for several reasons. This article will help you understand why this happens and how to resolve it.

**Why Does This Happen?**

There are several reasons why parts of your page might not appear in your heatmap:

**1\. Dynamic Content:** If your page contains content that loads dynamically (e.g., through JavaScript), it may not be captured in the initial page load.

**2\. Lazy Loading:** Elements that are lazy-loaded (only loaded when scrolled into view) might not be captured if they weren't in view when the heatmap was generated.

**3\. Iframe Content:** Content within iframes may not always be captured accurately in heatmaps.

**4\. Pop-ups or Overlays:** Elements that appear after user interaction might not be included in the initial heatmap.

**5\. Recent Page Changes:** If you've recently updated your page, the heatmap might be showing an older version.

**6\. Scrolling Issues:** In some cases, the heatmap might not capture the full length of a scrollable page.

**How to Fix It:**

To ensure your entire page is visible in the heatmap, try these solutions:

1\. Reload the Heatmap:

\- Go to your heatmap page.

\- Look for an option to "toggle interactive mode"

\- This will generate a reload your heatmap based on the current state of your page.

2\. Check for JavaScript Conflicts:

\- Ensure that your page's JavaScript isn't interfering with the heatmap script.

\- Temporarily disable other scripts to see if it resolves the issue.

3\. Check Browser Compatibility:

\- Try viewing the heatmap in a different browser to rule out browser-specific issues.

**Still Having Issues?**

If you've tried these solutions and are still experiencing problems, gather the following information and contact our support team:

\- The URL of the page with the issue

\- Screenshots of what you're seeing in the heatmap vs. what you expect to see

\- Any recent changes made to the page

\- The browsers and devices where you're experiencing the problem

Our team will be happy to help you troubleshoot and ensure your heatmaps are capturing your entire page accurately.

Remember, accurate heatmaps are crucial for making informed decisions about your website's design and user experience. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need further assistance!

# How to Apply and Use Filters for Screen Recordings in Heatmap? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024085-how-to-apply-and-use-filters-for-screen-recordings-in-heatmap#main-content)

How to Apply and Use Filters for Screen Recordings in Heatmap?
==============================================================

screen recordings, filters, user segments, date range, device type, session duration, user behavior, custom events, filter management

October 21, 2024

**How to Apply and Use Filters for Screen Recordings in Heatmap?**

Screen recordings provide valuable insights into user behavior on your website. To make the most of this feature, Heatmap allows you to apply filters to narrow down and focus on specific user sessions. This guide will walk you through the process of applying and using filters for your screen recordings.

Why Use Filters?

Filters help you:

\- Focus on specific user segments

\- Analyze behavior based on particular criteria

\- Save time by viewing only relevant recordings

Applying Filters to Screen Recordings:

1\. Navigate to the Screen Recordings section in your Heatmap dashboard.

2\. Look for the "Filters" option, typically located near the top of the page.

3\. Click on "Add Filter" to see the available filter options.

4\. Choose from a variety of filters, such as:

\- Date Range

\- Device Type (Desktop, Mobile, Tablet)

\- Browser

\- Country

\- Pages Visited

\- Session Duration

\- User Behavior (e.g., Rage Clicks, U-Turns)

\- Custom Events

5\. Select the desired filter and set the specific criteria.

6\. Click "Apply" to activate the filter.

7\. Your screen recordings list will now update to show only the sessions that match your filter criteria.

Using Multiple Filters:

You can combine multiple filters to create more specific segments:

1\. After applying your first filter, click "Add Filter" again.

2\. Choose another filter category and set its criteria.

3\. Repeat this process to add as many filters as needed.

4\. Heatmap will display recordings that match ALL the selected filter criteria.

**Saving and Managing Filters:**

\- To save a set of filters for future use, look for a "Save Filter" or "Create Segment" option.

\- Give your saved filter a name for easy reference.

\- Access saved filters from the Filters menu to quickly apply them in the future.

**Removing Filters:**

\- To remove a single filter, click the "X" next to the filter name.

\- To clear all filters, look for a "Clear All" or "Reset Filters" option.

**Tips for Effective Filter Use:**

1\. Start with broad filters and gradually narrow down to find specific user behaviors.

2\. Use date range filters to analyze how user behavior changes over time.

3\. Combine device type and behavior filters to understand how different users interact with your site.

4\. Regularly review and update your saved filters to ensure they remain relevant.

By effectively using filters, you can gain deeper insights from your screen recordings and make data-driven decisions to improve your website's user experience.

If you need further assistance with using filters for screen recordings, please don't hesitate to contact our support team.

# Why does my dashboard show "snippet not configured" when it's verified? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024038-why-does-my-dashboard-show-snippet-not-configured-when-it-s-verified#main-content)

Why does my dashboard show "snippet not configured" when it's verified?
=======================================================================

snippet not configured, browser caching, low traffic, delayed data processing, heatmap snippet, troubleshooting, traffic inactivity

October 21, 2024

**Why does my dashboard show "snippet not configured" when it's verified?**

Sometimes you may notice that your dashboard displays a "snippet not configured" message even though you've successfully verified your heatmap tracking snippet. This can be confusing and concerning, but there are a few reasons why this might occur:

1.  **Browser Caching**
    

Your browser might be showing a cached version of your dashboard. Try clearing your browser cache and reloading the page to see if this resolves the issue.

1.  **Low Traffic or Inactivity**
    

The heatmap snippet works by sending data to our servers when user activities occur on your site. If your site has very low traffic or there hasn't been any recent activity, the lack of data transmission might trigger a false "not configured" status.

1.  **Delayed Data Processing**
    

There can sometimes be a slight delay between data collection and processing. This might cause a temporary discrepancy between the actual snippet status and what's displayed on your dashboard.

**Troubleshooting Steps:**

1.  Wait for a few hours and check again. The status often updates automatically within this timeframe.
    
2.  Ensure your site is receiving some traffic. You can visit the site yourself to generate some activity.
    
3.  Clear your browser cache and reload the dashboard.
    
4.  Verify that the snippet is still correctly installed on your site.
    

If the issue persists after trying these steps, it's possible there may be a system anomaly. In this case, please contact our support team for further assistance. We'll be happy to investigate and resolve any underlying issues.

Remember, even if the dashboard shows this message temporarily, it doesn't necessarily mean your data isn't being collected. As long as the snippet is correctly installed, data collection should continue uninterrupted.

**Where Can I Check My Verification Snippet Status?**

1\. In Your Heatmap Account:

\- Go to the Dashboard

\- Find the "Snippet Status" section at the top

This shows:

\- Verification status (Verified or Inactive)

\- Performance for the last 30 days

\- Duration of site verification

2\. Manually Checking Your Website:

\- Open your website in a web browser

\- Right-click and select "View Page Source" or press Ctrl+U (Cmd+U on Mac)
