\- Right-click and select "Inspect" or press F12

\- Go to the "Network" tab

\- Refresh the page

\- Look for requests to "heatmap.com" or containing your Heatmap ID

If you can't find the snippet or are having issues:

\- Verify the snippet is correctly installed

\- Check for script conflicts

\- Contact our support team for assistance

Regular verification ensures accurate data collection for your heatmaps.

# Why Do Pages Look Broken or Have No CSS Loading in Heatmap? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024089-why-do-pages-look-broken-or-have-no-css-loading-in-heatmap#main-content)

Why Do Pages Look Broken or Have No CSS Loading in Heatmap?
===========================================================

broken pages, missing CSS, Heatmap access, whitelist IP, geolocation restrictions, domain blocking, referrer blocking, cookie policies

October 21, 2024

**Why Do Pages Look Broken or Have No CSS Loading in Heatmap?**

If you've noticed that your pages appear broken or are missing CSS styling when viewed in Heatmap, don't worry. This is a common issue that can usually be resolved quickly. This article will explain why this happens and how to fix it.

**Why Does This Happen?**

Heatmap needs to access your website's assets, including CSS files, to generate accurate heatmaps and recordings. When pages look broken or CSS isn't loading properly, it typically means our servers are having trouble fetching some of the CSS files from your server.

**Common Causes:**

1\. Geolocation restrictions: Your site may only allow access from specific geographic locations.

2\. IP restrictions: Your server may only allow specific IP addresses to access assets.

3\. Domain/referrer blocking: Your site may block requests from unknown domains or referrers.

4\. Cookie/session storage restrictions: Your site may require cookies or session storage to serve assets.

**How to Fix It:**

To resolve this issue, you'll need to allow Heatmap's servers to access your CSS files. Here are the steps to take:

1\. Whitelist Heatmap IP Addresses:

\- Contact Heatmap support to obtain the list of IP addresses used by our servers.

\- Add these IP addresses to your server's whitelist or firewall rules.

2\. Allow Heatmap Domain/Referrer:

\- Add the Heatmap domain (provided by support) to your list of allowed domains or referrers.

3\. Review Cookie and Session Policies:

\- If your site requires cookies or session storage to serve assets, you may need to adjust these settings to allow Heatmap access.

4\. Check Geolocation Restrictions:

\- Ensure that your geolocation restrictions aren't blocking Heatmap's servers.

After making these changes, refresh your Heatmap dashboard and check if the issue is resolved. If you're still experiencing problems, please contact our support team for further assistance.

Note: Always ensure that allowing access for Heatmap doesn't compromise your site's overall security. If you have any concerns, consult with your IT security team before making changes.

By following these steps, you should be able to resolve issues with broken pages or missing CSS in Heatmap, allowing you to get the most accurate and useful data from our tools.

If you need any additional help or have questions, please don't hesitate to reach out to our support team.

# A/B Test Filters | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10572363-a-b-test-filters#main-content)

A/B Test Filters
================

View Data from both Live and Ended A/B Tests in Heatmap

Updated this week

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10572363-a-b-test-filters#h_679ffbecb0)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10572363-a-b-test-filters#h_2fbaa7ed7a)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10572363-a-b-test-filters#h_b0534df6e9)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10572363-a-b-test-filters#h_fe46ad35e6)

Pulling heatmap data from past A/B tests lets you see exactly how users interacted with each variant. This helps you understand what worked, what didn’t, and apply those insights to future improvements.

In Heatmap, you're able to pull data on both Live and Ended A/B Tests.

**Analyzing Data on A/B Tests within Heatmap**
==============================================

**If the A/B Test is Live:**
----------------------------

For tests that are still active and running, you'll be able to bring them into the A/B Test Filter as long as your testing platform is properly integrated with Heatmap.

Below are the A/B Test Integrations that we support and the necessary integration documentation:

*   [Shoplift Integration](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060151-a-b-test-filters-shoplift-integration)
    
*   [Visually Integration](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060368-a-b-test-filters-visually-integration)
    
*   [Intelligems Integration](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060523-a-b-test-filters-intelligems-integration)
    

To pull in your A/B test variants,

1.  Go to **Filters**, select **A/B Tests**.
    
2.  Select the **A/B testing tool** you're using to run the experiment, and then choose the specific **experiment name or variant** you'd like to bring into the platform**.**
    
    1.  **_Note:_** Heatmap will bring in the same naming conventions used in your A/B testing platform.
        
    
3.  Once you have the appropriate variant selected, click **Apply** and the page will reload with data from your A/B test.
    

**If the test has ended:**
--------------------------

Since the variants won’t be live anymore, we'll need to use the **date filter** and **View Previous Versions** feature to populate the appropriate data from your past A/B test.

1.  Go to the **Heatmap** feature and find the specific page you'd like to review.
    
2.  Use the **date picker** at the top of the screen to choose the time range you want to review and click View Previous Versions.
    
3.  Select the appropriate display you'd like to analyze and click **Load Selected Version** to populate the data.
    
4.  Heatmap will re-load the page with the appropriate display and provide visual data (clicks, scroll depth, etc.) for that version of the page.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1665603746/70f782866c4413dc4792e2f2c1b8/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=68016632a95cce3526025a4f8dea885b2245c9f54702473a2364b84dbfe54486&req=dSYhE89%2BnoZbX%2FMW1HO4zVgmlsBXE6gZzwZ7WeiHUWiRk3krQ7HVIEPT3LSf%0AeW%2FKVYC%2BPiixzFZ2Pv4%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1665603746/70f782866c4413dc4792e2f2c1b8/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=68016632a95cce3526025a4f8dea885b2245c9f54702473a2364b84dbfe54486&req=dSYhE89%2BnoZbX%2FMW1HO4zVgmlsBXE6gZzwZ7WeiHUWiRk3krQ7HVIEPT3LSf%0AeW%2FKVYC%2BPiixzFZ2Pv4%3D%0A)

**Heatmap <> Pack Digital Integration Guide**
=============================================

If you're A/B testing through Pack Digital, we can set up a partial-integration for you to be able to review your test data in Heatmap.

**Requirements**
----------------

*   Heatmap scripts **must be installed and running** on your site.
    
*   The snippet should run **after a variant has been selected**.
    
*   This integration provides **partial compatibility** - _we're currently working on an official integration with Pack Digital._
    

Note: Native variant previews in Heatmap Interactive Mode are not currently supported. A previous-version bypass may still work for previews.

**Required Parameters**
-----------------------

The following fields are required:

*   partner
    
*   experiment\_id
    
*   experiment\_name
    
*   variant\_id
    

variant\_preview\_url is **experimental** and optional.

variants is optional but recommended.

**Do I need to add any code?**
------------------------------

**Yes, you'll need to add this implementation snippet JavaScript to your experiment code:**

if (typeof window.heatmap\_set\_event\_tag === 'function') {  
  window.heatmap\_set\_event\_tag({  
    partner: partnerName,  
    experiment\_id: experimentId,  
    experiment\_name: experimentName,  
    variant\_id: activeVariantId,  
    variations: variationsArray,  
    // Optional / Experimental  
    variant\_preview\_url: variantPreviewUrl,  
  });  
}

**Example implementation code:**

if (typeof window.heatmap\_set\_event\_tag === 'function') {  
  window.heatmap\_set\_event\_tag({  
    partner: "packdigital",  
    experiment\_id: "pd-exp-1024",  
    experiment\_name: "Homepage Hero CTA Test",  
    variant\_id: "variant-b",  
    variations: \[  \
      { id: "variant-a", name: "Control" },  \
      { id: "variant-b", name: "New CTA Copy" }  \
    \],  
    variant\_preview\_url: "https://www.example.com/?preview\_variant=variant-b"  
  });  
}

* * *

Viewing A/B Test Variants
=========================

​Currently, Pack Digital is not a fully integrated provider with Heatmap, so viewing variant data in Heatmap requires manual interaction. The page preview does not automatically switch to the active variant unless an experimental preview URL is configured.

Step-by-Step Guide
------------------

### Set up A/B Testing Filter

1.  Log in to your Heatmap account
    
2.  Open **Heatmap View**:
    
    1.  Select Heatmap from the left sidebar
        
    2.  Choose a page from the Heatmaps list
        
    
3.  Click **Filters**, then select **A/B Tests**
    
4.  Choose your A/B testing platform from the dropdown
    
5.  Select the experiment or specific variant you want to analyze.
    
6.  Click **Apply**.
    

### Manual Steps to View the Variant

*   The heatmap page view will not automatically change to the selected variant.
    
*   The view may update automatically only if the experimental **variant\_preview\_url** is configured in the integration.
    
*   If the preview URL is **not** set, continue with the manual steps below.
    
    1.  Open the **Date Filter** and select a date range where the chosen variant has collected data.
        
    2.  Click **View Previous Versions**.
        
    3.  Select the page preview that most closely matches the variant you want to review.
        
    

### What You Will See

After completing the manual steps, the Heatmap will display:

*   A screenshot of the selected variant view for the chosen date range
    
*   Click heatmaps from visitors who saw that variant
    
*   Scroll and movement data specific to that variant
    
*   The variant name as configured in the integration
    
*   Total visit counts for the variant, broken down by device type
    

* * *

**Troubleshooting Common Issues**
=================================

### **What does this integration do?**

The Pack Digital A/B Testing integration allows experiment and variant data to be sent to Heatmap so sessions, clicks, and behavior can be analyzed by experiment variant.

* * *

### **Is Pack Digital fully compatible with Heatmap?**

Pack Digital is **partially compatible** with Heatmap at this time. Core experiment and variant tracking is supported, but some advanced features have limitations.

* * *

### **Do I need to install anything?**

Yes. Heatmap scripts must already be installed and running on your site before the Pack Digital integration code is added.

* * *

### **What data is required for the integration to work?**

The following fields are required:

*   Partner name
    
*   Experiment ID
    
*   Experiment name
    
*   Variant ID
    

If any of these are missing, Heatmap may not correctly associate sessions with your experiment.

* * *

### **Can I preview variants in Heatmap?**

Native variant previews in **Heatmap Interactive Mode** are not currently supported with this integration.

A preview URL can be passed, but it is **experimental** and may not always work as expected. Some customers may continue using a previous-version bypass for preview workflows.

* * *

### **Why is my experiment not showing up in Heatmap?**

Common reasons include:

*   Heatmap scripts are not loading correctly
    
*   The integration code runs before a variant is selected
    
*   Required parameters (such as variant\_id) are missing or undefined
    

* * *

### **Does this affect site performance?**

No. The integration sends lightweight metadata to Heatmap and does not block page rendering when implemented correctly.

* * *

### **Can I use this with multiple experiments at once?**

Yes, as long as each experiment sends a unique experiment ID and variant ID.

* * *

### **Is the integration stable?**

Yes for core tracking. However, some fields (such as preview URLs) are **experimental** and may change as the integration evolves.

* * *

### **Who should I contact if something doesn’t work?**

If issues persist after verifying setup, contact Heatmap support and include:

*   Experiment ID
    
*   Variant ID
    
*   Page URL where the issue occurs
    
*   Any relevant console errors
    

Reach out to [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 - we're here to help you succeed.

**Getting Started**
===================

**What are pop-up surveys?**
----------------------------

Pop-up surveys are on-site questionnaires that appear to visitors while they browse your website. They allow you to collect feedback, understand user intent, and gather insights about the visitor experience in real-time.

**How do I create my first pop-up survey?**
-------------------------------------------

Navigate to the Surveys section in your Heatmap.com dashboard, click "Create Survey," and choose "Pop-up Survey." You'll be guided through selecting your survey type, customizing questions, and setting display rules.

**What types of pop-up surveys can I create?**
----------------------------------------------

Heatmap.com supports several survey types including exit-intent surveys, NPS (Net Promoter Score) surveys, customer satisfaction surveys, micro-surveys, and custom feedback forms. Each type is optimized for different use cases and visitor journeys.

**Implementation & Technical Setup**
====================================

**Do I need to install additional code for pop-up surveys?**
------------------------------------------------------------

No additional code is required. Pop-up surveys work through your existing Heatmap.com tracking script. Once you create and activate a survey, it will automatically appear to visitors based on your targeting rules.

**Will pop-up surveys slow down my website?**
---------------------------------------------

Pop-up surveys are designed to load asynchronously and have minimal impact on page performance. The survey content loads after your page has rendered, ensuring your site speed remains unaffected.

**Can I preview surveys before making them live?**
--------------------------------------------------

Yes, you can preview surveys in the editor under “Interactive Preview” to see exactly how they'll appear to visitors without affecting your data or showing surveys to actual users.

**Are pop-up surveys mobile-responsive?**
-----------------------------------------

All pop-up surveys automatically adapt to different screen sizes and devices. The interface is optimized for desktop, tablet, and mobile experiences to ensure high completion rates across all devices.

**Is there a limit to how many surveys I can create?**
------------------------------------------------------

There’s no limit to how many surveys you can create; however, you can only publish one pop-up survey at a time.

**Targeting & Display Rules**
=============================

**How do I control when and where surveys appear?**
---------------------------------------------------

You can control both the timing and placement of your survey under the **"Define Your Survey's Behavior"** and **"Choose Where This Survey Shows"** steps when creating or editing your survey.

**Timing (Define Your Survey's Behavior)**: choose when the survey appears:

*   Show immediately after page load
    
*   Show after a specific time delay
    
*   Show when a visitor is about to abandon (exit intent)
    
*   Show after scrolling a specific percentage of the page
    

**Placement (Choose Where This Survey Shows)**: choose where the survey appears:

*   **Show on all pages of my site**: your survey will appear across your entire site.
    
*   **Show only on pages that match a rule**: your survey will only appear on the specific page(s) you choose. Select your rule type (e.g. "URL ends with") and enter the page URL you want to target. You can add multiple rules if you want to target more than one page.
    

**Can I show different surveys to different audience segments?**
----------------------------------------------------------------

Currently, it’s not possible to segment pop-up surveys to different audience groups.

**Can I trigger surveys based on specific user actions?**
---------------------------------------------------------

Yes, you can trigger surveys based on events like initial page load, percentage of scroll depth, delayed time on page, or exit intent tracked through your implementation.

**Survey Design & Customization**
=================================

**Can I customize the appearance of my surveys?**
-------------------------------------------------

You have the ability to change colors, fonts, and button styles. Surveys can match your website's design system to create a seamless experience.

**What question types are available?**
--------------------------------------

Heatmap.com supports multiple question types including multiple choice, rating scales, open-ended text responses, single choice, and multi-select checkboxes.

**How many questions can I include in a pop-up survey?**
--------------------------------------------------------

To follow best practices, you’ll have the ability to ask one question in the pop-up survey.

**Data & Analysis**
===================

**Where can I view survey responses?**
--------------------------------------

All responses are available in the Surveys section of your dashboard. You can view individual responses under the specific survey you’d like to analyze.

**How quickly does survey data appear in my dashboard?**
--------------------------------------------------------

Survey responses appear in real-time. As soon as a visitor submits a survey, the data is immediately available in your dashboard and reports.

**Can I export survey results?**
--------------------------------

Yes, you can export survey data as CSV or PDF. Exports include all response data, timestamps, and associated metadata like device type and traffic source.

**Privacy & Compliance**
========================

**Do surveys collect personal information?**
--------------------------------------------

Surveys only collect the information you explicitly request in your questions. Heatmap.com does not automatically collect personally identifiable information.

**Can visitors opt out of surveys?**
------------------------------------

Yes, all surveys include a close button, and visitors can dismiss them at any time.

**Best Practices**
==================

**What's a good response rate for pop-up surveys?**
---------------------------------------------------

Response rates vary by survey type and implementation, but typical rates range from 2% to 15%. Exit-intent surveys and short micro-surveys typically achieve higher response rates than lengthy forms.

**When is the best time to show a survey?**
-------------------------------------------

Timing depends on your goals. Exit-intent surveys work well for understanding why visitors are leaving. Mid-session surveys after 30-60 seconds can capture feedback from engaged users. Post-action surveys after purchases or form submissions gather timely insights.

**How can I increase survey completion rates?**
-----------------------------------------------

Keep surveys short, make questions clear and specific, explain why you're asking for feedback, offer incentives when appropriate, ensure mobile optimization, and avoid interrupting critical user flows like checkout processes.

**Should I offer incentives for completing surveys?**
-----------------------------------------------------

Incentives can increase response rates but may affect response quality. Consider your goals: if you need volume, incentives help. If you want feedback from genuinely engaged users, surveys without incentives often yield more thoughtful responses.

**Troubleshooting**
===================

**My survey isn't appearing on my website. What should I check?**
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Verify that your Heatmap.com tracking script is installed correctly and the survey is set to "Published" status. If you’re still running into issues, please reach out to Customer Support at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

**Can surveys conflict with my website's pop-ups or chat widgets?**
-------------------------------------------------------------------

Heatmap.com surveys are designed to play nicely with other on-site tools. You can adjust z-index values and positioning to ensure surveys don't overlap with existing elements.

**How do I stop a survey from displaying?**
-------------------------------------------

You can pause or deactivate any survey from the dashboard by clicking the three dots and selecting “Unpublished.” Paused surveys stop displaying immediately but retain all existing data and settings for later reactivation.

**Why are my response rates lower than expected?**
--------------------------------------------------

Low response rates can result from surveys appearing too quickly, being too long, having unclear questions, poor targeting, appearing on mobile devices without optimization, or showing too frequently to the same visitors. Review your survey design and targeting settings.

* * *

**Need More Help?**
-------------------

If you have questions not covered in this FAQ, please contact our support team at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

# How to Use Comparison Mode for Heatmaps? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024076-how-to-use-comparison-mode-for-heatmaps#main-content)

How to Use Comparison Mode for Heatmaps?
========================================

comparison mode, Heatmap, user segments, behavior analysis, A/B testing, time period comparison, filter comparison, design changes

October 21, 2024

**How to Use Comparison Mode for Heatmaps?**

Comparison mode is a powerful feature in Heatmap that allows you to compare data from two different filters side by side. This tool provides valuable insights into how different user segments interact with your website. Here's a comprehensive guide on how to use this feature effectively.

**Why Use Comparison Mode?**

Comparison mode helps you:

\- Analyze behavior differences between user segments

\- Compare performance across different time periods

\- Evaluate the impact of design changes or A/B tests

\- Identify optimization opportunities based on user behavior patterns

**How to Access and Use Comparison Mode:**

1\. Accessing Comparison Mode:

\- Navigate to your heatmap area in the dashboard

\- Select your first filter

\- Click the "Compare" button (usually located near the filter options)

\- Choose your second filter

\- Click "Apply" to generate the comparison

2\. Viewing Comparison Results:

\- Two heatmaps will load side by side, each applying one of the selected filters

\- The left heatmap represents your first filter, and the right represents the second

\- You can interact with both heatmaps independently

3\. Analyzing Specific Elements:

\- Click on any element in either heatmap to open a data modal

\- This modal will show a side-by-side comparison of that element's performance under both filters

\- You'll see metrics such as clicks, conversions, and engagement for each filter

4\. Using the Data Table in Comparison Mode:

\- Open the Data Table view while in comparison mode

\- Each element will have an expand arrow beneath it

\- Click the arrow to reveal a detailed comparison of the element's performance under both filters

\- This view provides a comprehensive breakdown of metrics for easy analysis

5\. Exporting Comparison Data:

\- Use the export function in the Data Table to download the comparative data

\- This allows for offline analysis or inclusion in reports

Tips for Effective Use of Comparison Mode:

1\. Compare similar time periods to identify seasonal trends or the impact of marketing campaigns

2\. Use device type filters to understand how behavior differs between mobile and desktop users

3\. Compare new vs. returning visitors to tailor your site for different user familiarity levels

4\. Analyze before and after periods when making significant site changes to measure impact

5\. Compare high-converting vs. low-converting segments to identify successful elements

**Common Use Cases:**

\- A/B Testing: Compare two versions of a page to see which performs better

\- Device Optimization: Analyze how mobile users interact with your site compared to desktop users

\- Geographic Analysis: Compare user behavior across different countries or regions

\- Time-Based Analysis: Evaluate how user behavior changes during different times of day or days of the week

**Troubleshooting:**

If you encounter any issues while using comparison mode:

\- Ensure both filters have sufficient data for a meaningful comparison

\- Check that the date ranges for both filters don't overlap if you're comparing different periods

\- Clear your browser cache or try a different browser if the comparison doesn't load properly

By leveraging comparison mode, you can gain deeper insights into your website's performance and make data-driven decisions to improve user experience and conversion rates. If you need further assistance with using comparison mode, don't hesitate to contact our support team.

# Why Are There Few or No Recordings Within 24 Hours of Subscribing? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024096-why-are-there-few-or-no-recordings-within-24-hours-of-subscribing#main-content)

Why Are There Few or No Recordings Within 24 Hours of Subscribing?
==================================================================

few recordings, no recordings, data collection, processing time, website traffic, script installation, script placement, recording settings

October 21, 2024

**Why Are There Few or No Recordings Within 24 Hours of Subscribing?**

If you've recently subscribed to heatmap and are seeing few or no recordings within the first 24 hours, don't be alarmed. This is a common situation with several potential explanations. Here's what you need to know:

1\. Data Collection and Processing Time

Heatmap needs time to collect and process data. While some data may appear quickly, it can take up to 24-48 hours for a significant number of recordings to be available.

2\. Website Traffic Volume

The number of recordings depends on your website's traffic. If your site has low traffic, it may take longer to accumulate a substantial number of recordings.

3\. Verify Script Installation

Ensure the heatmap tracking script is correctly installed on your website:

\- Log into your heatmap account

\- Go to the Settings or Installation section

\- Confirm your site shows as "Active" or "Verified"

4\. Check Script Placement

The tracking script should be placed in the <head> section of your website. Incorrect placement can delay or prevent data collection.

5\. Review Recording Settings

Check your recording settings to ensure they're configured to capture the data you're expecting:

\- Log into your heatmap account

\- Navigate to the Recording Settings section

\- Verify that the appropriate options are enabled

6\. Examine Sampling Rate

Heatmap may use sampling to manage data for high-traffic websites. Check your account settings to see if sampling is enabled and at what rate.

7\. Consider Time Zones

Remember that heatmap may use a different time zone than your local time. This could affect when you see new recordings appear.

8\. Look for Filtering Issues

Ensure you haven't accidentally applied any filters that might be excluding recordings from view.

9\. Check for Blocking Technologies

Some privacy tools or browser settings can block tracking scripts. Test your site in an incognito/private browsing window to rule this out.

10\. Verify Compatibility

Confirm that your website technology is fully compatible with heatmap. Some single-page applications or dynamically loaded content may require special configuration.

What to Do Next:

\- Wait at least 48 hours after proper installation before becoming concerned about low recording numbers.

\- Use this time to familiarize yourself with other heatmap features and set up your dashboard.

\- If you continue to see no recordings after 48 hours, and you've verified your installation, please contact our support team.

When contacting support, please provide:

\- Your website URL

\- Confirmation that you've verified the script installation

\- Your typical daily traffic volume

\- Any error messages you've encountered

Remember, our team is here to help ensure you get the most out of heatmap. We're committed to helping you gather valuable insights about your website visitors as quickly as possible.

# How to Filter for Purchasers vs Non-Purchasers | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024108-how-to-filter-for-purchasers-vs-non-purchasers#main-content)

How to Filter for Purchasers vs Non-Purchasers
==============================================

purchasers vs non-purchasers, purchase filter, conversion behavior, user behavior, comparison mode, conversion optimization

October 21, 2024

**How to Filter for Purchasers vs Non-Purchasers**

Heatmap allows you to easily compare the behavior of users who made a purchase versus those who didn't. This powerful filtering capability can provide valuable insights into what drives conversions on your site. Here's how to set it up:

1\. Open Your Heatmap

Navigate to the heatmap for the page you want to analyze.

2\. Access the Filters Menu

Look for the "Filters" option, typically located near the top of the heatmap view.

3\. Select the Purchase Filter

In the Filters menu, find the "Purchase" or "Conversion" filter option.

4\. Choose Purchasers

To view data for users who made a purchase, select "Purchasers" or "Converted" from the dropdown.

5\. Apply the Filter

Click "Apply" or "Update" to refresh the heatmap with data only from users who made a purchase.

6\. Analyze Purchaser Behavior

Take note of where purchasers click, how far they scroll, and which elements they interact with most.

7\. Switch to Non-Purchasers

Go back to the Filters menu and change the selection to "Non-Purchasers" or "Non-Converted".

8\. Apply the Filter Again

Click "Apply" to update the heatmap with non-purchaser data.

9\. Compare the Differences

Look for key differences in behavior between purchasers and non-purchasers. This can highlight areas for improvement or optimization.

10\. Use Comparison Mode (Optional)

For a side-by-side view, use Heatmap's Comparison Mode to see purchaser and non-purchaser data simultaneously.

Pro Tip: Combine the purchase filter with other filters like traffic source or device type for even more granular insights into user behavior.

By analyzing the differences between purchasers and non-purchasers, you can identify opportunities to improve your conversion funnel and optimize your site for better performance.

If you need any further assistance with filtering or interpreting your data, don't hesitate to reach out to our support team.

# Why Are My Screen Recordings Blank? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024100-why-are-my-screen-recordings-blank#main-content)

Why Are My Screen Recordings Blank?
===================================

blank screen recordings, browser extension, script installation, Content Security Policy, third-party integrations, cache, incognito mode, ad blockers, compatibility

October 21, 2024

**Why Are My Screen Recordings Blank?**

**If you're experiencing issues with blank screen recordings in heatmap, don't worry - this is usually caused by a few common factors that can be easily addressed. Here's what you need to know:**

**1\. Check Your Browser Extension**

**Make sure you have the latest version of the heatmap browser extension installed and enabled. Outdated or disabled extensions can cause recording issues.**

**2\. Verify Script Installation**

**Confirm that the heatmap tracking script is properly installed on your website. You can do this by:**

**\- Logging into your heatmap account**

**\- Going to the Settings or Installation section**

**\- Verifying that your site shows as "Active" or "Verified"**

**3\. Allow Sufficient Time for Data Collection**

**Screen recordings may not appear immediately after installation. Allow at least 24 hours for data to be collected and processed.**

**4\. Check Content Security Policy (CSP)**

**If your website has a strict Content Security Policy, it may block the recording script. Review your CSP settings and ensure they allow heatmap's domains.**

**5\. Examine Third-Party Integrations**

**Some third-party tools or plugins can interfere with screen recording. Temporarily disable them to see if this resolves the issue.**

**6\. Clear Browser Cache and Cookies**

**Sometimes, clearing your browser's cache and cookies can resolve display issues with recordings.**

**7\. Test in Incognito/Private Mode**

**Try viewing your recordings in an incognito or private browsing window to rule out any browser extension conflicts.**

**8\. Check for Ad Blockers**

**Ad blocking software can sometimes interfere with screen recording scripts. Try disabling any ad blockers on your site.**

**9\. Verify Compatibility**

**Ensure your website technology is compatible with heatmap's recording capabilities. Some single-page applications or dynamically loaded content may require special configuration.**

**10\. Review Privacy Settings**

**Make sure you haven't accidentally enabled any privacy settings that might prevent recordings from being captured or displayed.**

**If you've tried these steps and are still experiencing issues with blank screen recordings, please contact our support team. Provide the following information to help us troubleshoot:**

**\- Your website URL**

**\- The browser and version you're using**

**\- Any error messages you're seeing**

**\- Screenshots of the blank recordings (if possible)**

**Our team is here to help ensure you get the most out of your heatmap experience, including fully functional screen recordings to gain insights into user behavior on your site.**

# How to Distinguish Between Returning and New Users? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024135-how-to-distinguish-between-returning-and-new-users#main-content)

How to Distinguish Between Returning and New Users?
===================================================

new users, returning users, user segmentation, filter by user type, heatmap analysis, user behavior, conversion rates, traffic source

March 13, 2025

**How to Distinguish Between Returning and New Users?**

Heatmap allows you to segment your data based on user types, specifically differentiating between new and returning visitors. This distinction can provide valuable insights into how different user groups interact with your website. Here's how to use this feature:

**Understanding New vs Returning Users**

\- \*\*New Users\*\*: Visitors who are interacting with your website for the first time.

\- \*\*Returning Users\*\*: Visitors who have been to your website before and are coming back for another session.

**Steps to Filter by User Type**

1\. Log into your heatmap dashboard.

2\. Navigate to the heatmap or report you want to analyze.

3\. Look for the "Filters" option, typically located near the top of the page.

4\. Click on "Filters" to open the filtering menu.

5\. In the filtering menu, find the "User Type" or "Visitor Type" filter. This may be under a category like "User Behavior" or "Visit Information".

6\. Select "User Type" to add it as an active filter.

7\. You'll see options to choose between "New Users" and "Returning Users".

8\. Select the user type you want to analyze.

9\. Click "Apply" or "Save" to activate the filter.

10\. The heatmap and associated data will now update to show only sessions from the selected user type.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1421209854/895b9952be0a536aa85169a5ee9b/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=ecbb321ee53c44b14877acc96ebacc0c029f0b7f070bee03be30735156c67818&req=dSQlF8t%2BlIlaXfMW1HO4zR12ijKlbyAgFq3UYygQ9bn6Hoqd2hvA6wYLGXqx%0AIlg%2Bom2xOZXlIQpfRuA%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1421209854/895b9952be0a536aa85169a5ee9b/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=ecbb321ee53c44b14877acc96ebacc0c029f0b7f070bee03be30735156c67818&req=dSQlF8t%2BlIlaXfMW1HO4zR12ijKlbyAgFq3UYygQ9bn6Hoqd2hvA6wYLGXqx%0AIlg%2Bom2xOZXlIQpfRuA%3D%0A)

_Image above showing where to locate the New and Returning Users Filter_

**Analyzing New vs Returning User Data**

\- Compare heatmaps for new and returning users to see how familiarity with your site affects user behavior.

\- Look at metrics like time on site, pages viewed, and conversion rates for each user type.

\- Use these insights to tailor your site design and content to better serve both new and returning visitors.

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1421220848/e4524b64de14418e01e74c9171b1/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=fdd90e5772ba4aea5376402ee9a991360d14a505e03fe483a554247963493223&req=dSQlF8t8nYlbUfMW1HO4zU5YOL9rK%2FVNKMwjCy9pH%2B6RXHgloMtDBaSCsJmb%0ATLDhwPfbyMzkufIDB7E%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1421220848/e4524b64de14418e01e74c9171b1/image.png?expires=1789486200&signature=fdd90e5772ba4aea5376402ee9a991360d14a505e03fe483a554247963493223&req=dSQlF8t8nYlbUfMW1HO4zU5YOL9rK%2FVNKMwjCy9pH%2B6RXHgloMtDBaSCsJmb%0ATLDhwPfbyMzkufIDB7E%3D%0A)

_Image Showing how to use Compare mode for New and Returning Users. This feature works as well with any other filter option_

**Tips for Using User Type Filters**

\- Combine the User Type filter with other filters like device type or traffic source for more detailed analysis.

\- Consider creating separate heatmaps for new and returning users to easily compare them side by side.

\- Use the User Type filter in conjunction with conversion funnels to see how familiarity impacts your conversion process.

**Troubleshooting**

If you're having trouble distinguishing between new and returning users:

\- Ensure your heatmap tracking code is properly installed on all pages of your site.

\- Check that you haven't accidentally applied conflicting filters.

\- Verify that your site is correctly setting and reading cookies for user identification.

If you continue to experience issues with user type identification, please reach out to heatmap support for assistance.

# Why aren't my Heatmap's page elements showing any data? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#main-content)

Why aren't my Heatmap's page elements showing any data?
=======================================================

Importance of Unique Selector IDs for capturing data on Heatmap page elements

Updated this week

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#h_72c0feac17)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#h_c493f0504c)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#h_f0ed6b5318)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#h_c0be57815e)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#h_a5178b6d47)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#h_72053f8d04)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10508546-why-aren-t-my-heatmap-s-page-elements-showing-any-data#h_768cee2981)

If your site doesn't use unique selector IDs, even minor theme changes can break your heatmap data. When a heatmap can't "see" activity on specific buttons or links, the cause is usually shifting or ambiguous selectors (ie: reused classes, auto-generated names, or elements that move during A/B tests and SPA updates). Giving each key element a unique, stable selector (for example, an `id` or a dedicated `data-heatmap-id`) provides the tracker with a permanent anchor. That lets it consistently bind to the right element, distinguish look-alikes, and keep aggregating data even as layouts evolve. In the sections below, you'll learn how to add unique selectors, confirm they're being captured, and troubleshoot edge cases like dynamic content, modals, and iframes.

This article answers common questions about Unique Selector IDs. For a deeper "how-to" guide on what they are and how to implement them, see this [article](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10805821-complete-guide-to-unique-selector-ids-for-website-analytics)
.

Getting Started
===============

### What are unique selector IDs and why do I need them?

Unique selector IDs are persistent, descriptive identifiers assigned to HTML elements that ensure your website elements remain consistently trackable even after updates or changes. Unlike generic class names, unique IDs prevent data loss and maintain accurate analytics across your site's evolution.

### How do I know if my website needs unique IDs?

Open your browser's Developer Tools, inspect key elements like product cards, navigation items, or buttons. If you don't see an `id=""` attribute, that element lacks a unique identifier and could cause tracking issues.

### What's the difference between regular IDs and data-heatmap-id?

Both serve the same tracking purpose. Use standard `id` attributes when possible, but `data-heatmap-id` is available as an alternative when page builders, CMS limitations, or existing ID conflicts prevent using standard IDs.

Implementing Unique IDs
=======================

### Which elements should have unique IDs first?

**High Priority:** Product cards, navigation menus, call-to-action buttons, forms, checkout elements, sliders, and featured sections.

**Medium Priority:** Footer sections, social links, testimonials, and informational blocks.

### What makes a good unique ID name?

Use descriptive, structured names that clearly identify the element's purpose. Good examples: `bestseller-product-1`, `main-navigation-header`, `newsletter-signup-form`. Avoid generic names like `section1` or randomly generated numbers.

### Can I add IDs without touching code?

This depends on your platform. WordPress page builders like Elementor have ID fields in their interfaces. Webflow has built-in ID fields in Element Settings. However, most platforms require some template-level editing for comprehensive implementation.

### Will my IDs survive theme updates?

Not automatically. Create a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) that documents all your ID implementations. After theme updates, you'll need to re-implement IDs using your documentation as a reference.

### How do I handle dynamic content like product loops?

Use your platform's templating system to create dynamic IDs. For example, in Shopify: `id="product-{{ product.id }}"` or in loops: `id="collection-item-{{ forloop.index }}"`. This ensures each element gets a unique identifier automatically.

### Should I use numbers in my ID names?

Use meaningful numbers that relate to your content (like product IDs), but avoid random numbers. Good: `featured-product-123`, Bad: `element-847291`. The ID should make sense to someone reading your code.

### How often should I audit my IDs?

Check your IDs during initial setup, after theme updates, before major site changes, and when adding new functionality. Regular audits help catch issues before they affect your data.

### What naming convention should I use?

Use kebab-case (hyphens) for readability: `main-navigation-item` rather than `mainNavigationItem` or `main_navigation_item`. Keep names descriptive but concise.

### Can I change an ID after it's been implemented?

Yes, but be aware that changing IDs will create a break in your historical data. If you must change an ID, document the change and consider the impact on your analytics continuity.

### What are the most common ID implementation mistakes?

*   Using auto-generated random numbers that change
    
*   Creating duplicate IDs across elements
    
*   Making names too generic (`section1`, `product`)
    
*   Forgetting to update IDs after copying elements
    
*   Not documenting ID implementations for future reference
    

### Should every element on my page have a unique ID?

No, focus on elements important for tracking, user interaction, or accessibility. Over-implementing IDs can make your HTML cluttered. Prioritize interactive elements, navigation, products, forms, and key content sections.

### Is it okay to copy and paste elements with IDs?

Never copy elements with IDs without changing the ID to be unique. This creates duplicate IDs, which breaks HTML standards and can cause tracking and JavaScript issues.

* * *

Platform-Specific Questions
===========================

### How do I implement IDs on Shopify?

Shopify doesn't provide unique IDs by default. You'll need to edit template files (like `product-template.liquid`) and add IDs using Liquid syntax: `<div id="product-{{ product.id }}">` or use the data attribute alternative: `<div data-heatmap-id="product-{{ product.id }}">`.

### What about WordPress? Do I need to edit theme files?

For comprehensive coverage, yes. Edit template files directly or through a child theme. Many page builders also offer custom ID fields that can handle individual elements without code editing.

* * *

Troubleshooting
===============

### My tracking data disappeared after a site update. What happened?

This typically occurs when elements lose their unique IDs during updates. The tracking system can no longer identify elements consistently. Implement permanent, meaningful IDs to prevent this issue.

### I'm seeing duplicate ID errors in my browser console. How do I fix this?

Audit your site for duplicate IDs using Developer Tools. Each ID must be unique across your entire website. Use dynamic generation (like product IDs or loop indices) to ensure uniqueness, especially in repeated elements.

### My JavaScript stopped working after adding IDs. What went wrong?

Check if your JavaScript code relies on specific selectors that changed. Ensure your new IDs don't conflict with existing JavaScript. If you're using common names, consider more specific identifiers.

### How do I maintain IDs across a large website?

Create a documentation system that tracks all implemented IDs. Establish naming conventions and train your team on proper implementation. Consider creating templates or snippets for commonly used ID patterns.

* * *

Analytics and Tracking
======================

### How do unique IDs improve my heatmap data?

Unique IDs ensure Heatmap.com can consistently track elements even after site changes. Without them, data ties to element positions instead of the elements themselves, making insights unreliable after updates.

### What's the difference between continuous and experiment-based tracking?

Heatmap.com uses continuous tracking, automatically monitoring changes without manual intervention. Unique IDs ensure this system maintains consistent data. Other tools use experiment-based tracking that requires manual updates after changes.

### Will unique IDs affect my site's loading speed?

Actually, they improve performance. JavaScript can select elements directly by ID rather than traversing complex CSS selectors, making your scripts faster and more efficient.

### How do unique IDs help with A/B testing?

They ensure test variations target the exact same elements consistently, providing reliable results. Without unique IDs, testing tools might target different elements by mistake, skewing your data.

* * *

Getting Help
============

### What if I'm not comfortable editing code myself?

Contact your web developer or Heatmap.com support at [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
. Many implementations can be handled by developers familiar with your platform, and support can provide platform-specific guidance.

### How do I know if my implementation is working correctly?

Use your browser's Developer Tools to inspect elements and verify IDs are present and unique. Check your heatmap data for consistent tracking. Look for JavaScript console errors that might indicate ID conflicts.

### Where can I get platform-specific help?

*   **WordPress:** WordPress Documentation and theme developer resources
    
*   **Shopify:** Shopify Partner documentation and theme development guides
    
*   **Webflow:** Webflow University and their extensive documentation
    

For a Complete Guide on Unique Selector IDs, feel free to read our documentation [here](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10805821-importance-of-unique-selector-ids-for-website-analytics)
.

* * *

**Need Help?**
--------------

If you have questions or run into any issues while using Heatmap, our support team is here to help. Contact us anytime at [Support@heatmap.com](mailto:Support@heatmap.com)
.

# A/B Test Filters: Shoplift Integration | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060151-a-b-test-filters-shoplift-integration#main-content)

A/B Test Filters: Shoplift Integration
======================================

Updated this week

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060151-a-b-test-filters-shoplift-integration#h_3915745113)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060151-a-b-test-filters-shoplift-integration#h_05e3c7b71c)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/12060151-a-b-test-filters-shoplift-integration#h_d3eb058fde)

Heatmap <> Shoplift Integration Guide
=====================================

We're excited to announce that heatmap now fully integrates with Shoplift, a powerful A/B testing and conversion optimization platform. This powerful combination allows you to analyze heatmap data for each of your test variants, helping you understand not just which variant performs better, but _why_ it performs better through visual behavior analysis.

Getting Started with heatmap + Shoplift
---------------------------------------

**What does this integration do?**

When you run A/B tests using Shoplift, heatmap automatically detects and tracks which variant each visitor sees. This enables you to:

*   View separate heatmaps for each variant
    
*   See exactly how users interact with different designs
    
*   Make data-driven decisions based on actual user behavior
    
*   Understand the "why" behind your test results
    

**Do I need to add any code?**  
No additional code is required! If you already have both heatmap and Shoplift installed on your website, the integration works automatically. We detect your Shoplift experiments and start tracking variant data immediately.

* * *

How to View Your Shoplift Test Data
-----------------------------------

### **Step-by-Step Guide:**

1.  Log into your Heatmap.com account.
    
2.  Navigate to your heatmap view.
    
3.  Click the "**Filter**" button.
    
4.  Select "**A/B Tests**" from the filter options.
    
5.  Choose "**Shoplift**" from the platform dropdown.
    
6.  Select your Shoplift experiment from the list.
    
7.  Choose the specific variant you want to analyze.
    
8.  Click "**Apply**" to view the filtered heatmap data.
    

#### **What you'll see:**

*   A screenshot of your selected variant
    
*   A heatmap of the click data from visitors who saw that variant
    
*   Scroll and movement data specific to that variant
    
*   The variant name as configured in Shoplift
    
*   Total visitor count for that variant (by device type)
    

* * *

Comparing Your Shoplift Variants
--------------------------------

Want to see how user behavior differs between your control and variant? Use our **Compare** feature:

1.  Select your first variant (following steps above).
    
2.  Instead of clicking "**Apply**", click "**Compare**".
    
3.  Select your second variant.
    
4.  View side-by-side behavioral differences.
    

This is perfect for understanding which design elements drive engagement and why certain variants outperform others.

* * *

Troubleshooting Common Issues
-----------------------------

#### → **"I don't see Shoplift in my filter options."**

*   First, verify:
    
    *   Your Shoplift experiment is actively running.
        
    *   You have traffic flowing to your variants.
        
    *   Both heatmap and Shoplift scripts are properly installed.
        
    
*   Then:
    
    *   Wait 1-2 hours after starting your experiment.
        
    *   Ensure you have sufficient traffic (at least 50+ visitors per variant).
        
    *   Check that your Shoplift experiment status is "Active."
        
    

#### → **"My variant preview doesn't look right."**

This can happen with dynamic content or personalized elements.

*   Solutions:
    
    *   Verify the variant displays correctly on your live site.
        
    *   Clear your browser cache and refresh.
        
    *   Check if you're using any dynamic elements that might not render in previews.
        
    *   Contact our support team with your experiment details.
        
    

#### → **"I see variant IDs instead of friendly names."**

We pull variant names directly from Shoplift.

*   To fix this:
    
    *   Ensure your variants have descriptive names in Shoplift.
        
    *   Allow 1-2 hours for name updates to sync.
        
    *   Refresh your heatmap.com dashboard.
        
    

#### → **"No data available for my variant."**

This typically means insufficient traffic to that variant.

*   Check:
    
    *   Your traffic split in Shoplift (ie: 50/50, 80/20).
        
    *   The variant is actively receiving visitors.
        
    *   Your experiment has been running long enough to collect data.
        
    *   The date range in heatmap matches your experiment timeline.
        
    

* * *

Best Practices for Shoplift Users
---------------------------------

#### Maximize your insights

*   **Run experiments for an adequate duration**
    
    *   We recommend at least 1,000 visitors per variant for meaningful heatmaps.
        
    *   Allow tests to run for complete business cycles (include weekends).  
        ​
        
    
*   **Use descriptive variant names in Shoplift**
    
    *   Instead of "Variant A," use "Blue CTA Button."
        
    *   This makes analysis much easier in Heatmap.com.  
        ​
        
    
*   **Focus on one major change per test**
    
    *   This makes it easier to identify what drives behavioral changes.
        
    *   Multiple changes can muddy your heatmap insights.  
        ​
        
    
*   **Document your hypotheses**
    
    *   Know what behavior changes you expect to see.
        
    *   Use heatmaps to validate or challenge these assumptions.
        
    

#### When to use heatmap data

*   **During tests:** Monitor for unexpected user behavior.
    
*   **After tests:** Understand why winners won and losers lost.
    
*   **For iteration:** Identify new test opportunities based on user behavior.
    

* * *

Understanding the Data
----------------------

#### **What we track for each Shoplift variant:**

*   All standard heatmap interactions (clicks, moves, scrolls)
    
*   Time spent on page
    
*   Rage clicks and dead clicks
    
*   Scroll depth
    
*   Hover patterns
    

#### **Data timing:**

*   Collection begins immediately when the experiment starts.
    
*   Variant data appears in filters within 1-2 hours.
    
*   Meaningful patterns emerge after 500+ visitors per variant.
    

#### **Important notes:**

*   Historical data before integration cannot be filtered by variant.
    
*   Each visitor is tracked with their assigned variant for their entire session.
    
*   Data is real-time (no delay once initial setup is complete).
    

* * *

Advanced Tips
-------------

#### **Analyzing test results:**

*   Look for unexpected click patterns between variants.
    
*   Compare scroll depth to understand content engagement.
    
*   Identify "dead zones" where no interaction occurs.
    
*   Watch for rage clicks indicating user frustration.
    

#### **Presenting findings:**

*   Use Compare mode for stakeholder presentations.
    
*   Export heatmap images for reports.
    
*   Combine with Shoplift's conversion data for a complete picture.
    

* * *

Getting Help
------------

**Need assistance?** For integration issues:

*   Verify both platforms are properly installed.
    
*   Check your Shoplift experiment is active.
    
*   Ensure adequate traffic to variants.
    

**When contacting support:**

*   Email: [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
    
*   Subject: "Shoplift Integration Support"
    
*   Please include:
    
    *   Your website URL
        
    *   Shoplift experiment name and ID
        
    *   Variant names
        
    *   When you started the experiment
        
    *   Screenshots of the variants
        
    *   Approximate traffic levels
        
    

We're here to help! Our support team is familiar with Shoplift and can help troubleshoot any integration issues. Most issues are resolved within 24 hours.

* * *

What's Next?
------------

**Coming soon:**

*   Compare filtered variants to overall traffic.
    
*   Enhanced preview capabilities.
    
*   Additional filtering options.
    
*   Export capabilities for variant comparisons.  
    ​
    

* * *

The heatmap and Shoplift integration represents a powerful combination for understanding not just what works, but why it works. We're excited to be part of your optimization journey!  
​

Questions? Reach out to [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
 - we're here to help you succeed.

# FAQ: Experiment Preview Links — Why They Break and How to Fix Them | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15518361-faq-experiment-preview-links-why-they-break-and-how-to-fix-them#main-content)

FAQ: Experiment Preview Links — Why They Break and How to Fix Them
==================================================================

June 16, 2026

Table of contents

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15518361-faq-experiment-preview-links-why-they-break-and-how-to-fix-them#h_5779f3dd9c)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15518361-faq-experiment-preview-links-why-they-break-and-how-to-fix-them#h_1dd38517e5)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15518361-faq-experiment-preview-links-why-they-break-and-how-to-fix-them#h_9472244ac9)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15518361-faq-experiment-preview-links-why-they-break-and-how-to-fix-them#h_cbf44315c1)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15518361-faq-experiment-preview-links-why-they-break-and-how-to-fix-them#h_3598ff8a0a)

[](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/15518361-faq-experiment-preview-links-why-they-break-and-how-to-fix-them#h_c4438cfc0c)

* * *

Overview
--------

When running A/B experiments through Heatmap.com, you rely on preview links to review your variant pages and analyze heatmap data without impacting live visitors. This article covers two common issues users run into:

1.  **Preview links that stop working** after an experiment is ended
    
2.  **Previews that load but look broken** — missing styles, images, or layout
    

Both are fixable. Here's everything you need to know.

* * *

Section 1: Why Did My Preview Links Stop Working?
-------------------------------------------------

What's happening?
-----------------

Preview links use the `?ig-preview=` URL parameter to load a specific experiment variant. This parameter needs an **active, live experiment** to hook into. The moment a test is ended, there's nothing for the parameter to connect to — so the link stops working.

This is by design, not a bug.

Why does it work this way?
--------------------------

The preview system is tied to the experiment's active state because it's pulling the correct variant configuration in real time. An ended experiment no longer has an active configuration to serve, so the preview has no source to load from.

* * *

Section 2: How to Keep Preview Links Working After You're Done Collecting Data
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pause the experiment instead of ending it
-----------------------------------------

This is the recommended approach. **Pausing** an experiment stops all live traffic from being assigned to test variants — but it keeps everything else intact:

*   Your experiment configuration is preserved
    
*   Your preview links remain functional
    
*   Your heatmap data stays accessible
    

You can continue analyzing variant performance through the Chrome extension or Heatmap dashboard without affecting any real users.

**To pause an experiment:**

1.  Go to your experiment in the dashboard
    
2.  Click **Pause** (not End)
    
3.  Your preview links will remain active immediately
    

End the experiment only when your analysis is fully complete and you no longer need access to the preview.

* * *

Section 3: My Test Is Already Ended — Can I Get My Preview Links Back?
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Yes. You'll need to briefly resume the experiment, then pause it right away. This restores the active state that the `?ig-preview=` parameter requires.

**Steps to restore preview access:**

1.  Find the ended experiment in your dashboard
    
2.  Click **Resume** — this reactivates the experiment briefly
    
3.  Immediately click **Pause** to stop live traffic from running again
    
4.  Your preview links will now work
    

**Note:** Between resuming and pausing, a small number of live visitors may temporarily be served the experiment variants. Pause as quickly as possible to minimize this.

* * *

Section 4: Quick Reference — End vs. Pause vs. Resume
-----------------------------------------------------

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Situation | Action |
| Finished collecting data, still analyzing | **Pause** |
| Analysis complete, no further access needed | **End** |
| Test ended too early, need previews back | **Resume → immediately Pause** |
| Want to run the test again from scratch | **Resume** |

* * *

Section 5: My Preview Loads, But the Page Looks Broken
------------------------------------------------------

This is a separate but related issue. Sometimes a preview link works — the variant loads — but the page looks visually broken: missing CSS, unstyled elements, images not loading, or a layout that doesn't match what visitors actually see.

Why does this happen?
---------------------

Heatmap's servers need to access your site's CSS and asset files to render the page accurately. If those files are blocked, the visual rendering will be incomplete or broken. Common causes include:

*   **Geolocation blocking** — your site restricts access to assets based on the visitor's region, and Heatmap's servers may be hitting that restriction
    
*   **Domain or referrer blocking** — your site only serves assets to requests from approved domains
    
*   **Cookie or sessionStorage dependencies** — some assets only load after a session has been initialized, which Heatmap's servers may not have
    

How to fix it
-------------

**Option 1: Whitelist Heatmap's IP addresses** Allow Heatmap's IP addresses in your server or CDN settings so our servers can fetch CSS and assets freely. See → [Heatmap IP Addresses](https://claude.ai/chat/6c756a8f-7d7a-40b1-9862-ceec4b177d46#)

**Option 2: Allow Heatmap's domain/referrer** Update your referrer-based access rules to allow requests originating from Heatmap's domain.

**Option 3: Check your Cloudflare settings** If you're using Cloudflare with Bot Fight Mode enabled, it may be blocking Heatmap's servers from fetching your assets. See → [Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode and Heatmap](https://claude.ai/chat/6c756a8f-7d7a-40b1-9862-ceec4b177d46#)

If the page still looks broken after trying these steps, contact our support team at **[support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
** with a description of the issue and the affected URL.

* * *

Section 6: Best Practices for Experiment Preview Management
-----------------------------------------------------------

*   **Always pause before analyzing.** Once you've called a test and stopped sending traffic, pause rather than end — you'll almost always want to go back and review the heatmap data.
    
*   **Don't end a test until you're fully done.** Reactivating an ended test to restore previews is possible, but it briefly re-exposes visitors to the experiment.
    
*   **Keep preview links saved.** Store your `?ig-preview=` URLs in your experiment notes or documentation so your team can access them without hunting.
    
*   **Use IP Blocking when reviewing previews.** If your team is reviewing variants and clicking around on preview links, those sessions will be tracked. Block your team's IP addresses to keep your heatmap data clean. See → [How to Set Up IP Blocking](https://claude.ai/chat/6c756a8f-7d7a-40b1-9862-ceec4b177d46#)

General Information
-------------------

**What are Customer Feedback Surveys?**
---------------------------------------

Customer Feedback Surveys are a powerful tool that allow you to gather insights directly from your customers. The better you understand your customers' needs and desires, the easier it is to create a high-converting website.  
​

Use surveys to better understand your customers' needs, preferences, and pain points, directly from the source.

**Why use Customer Feedback Surveys?**
--------------------------------------

Understanding your customers is key to growing your business. Your website copy, images, and messaging are the core to making a high-converting website, so your customers have the answers you need! Surveys are one of the fastest ways to make revenue-driving improvements to your website with very little effort.

With Customer Feedback Surveys, you can:  
​

*   Collect targeted feedback about specific products or experiences
    
*   Identify areas for improvement in the customer journey
    
*   “Crack the code” on your copywriting to better fit your customers
    
*   Determine why customers want your products over your competitors
    
*   Increase conversions by addressing customer concerns more effectively
    

* * *

**What question types can I include in my surveys?**
----------------------------------------------------

You can choose from a variety of question types:

*   Short-form text input  
    ​
    
    [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1481233475/47fdbad80a17fc4149185618b60a/AD_4nXcnGnEouPD5L_e9RVpEc7qIRW33PSfV4j2vL-Dd4AzoEpm5y5Has1FKjMaAA4_XeTXlJ0EhvvgC6WcbhM-gtFwiybI6xXSO3kA38Tdj_CJhOHkHTu4C_ydluSbIyZLb7Ftc85v6fg?expires=1789486200&signature=34b4eb6b9613c2e40a93e5c77af0fd2f74c5843bfa4fbb134ff9ef2ea11580fe&req=dSQvF8t9noVYXPMW1HO4zcJahpLMzejuvKYKJwypbrOdnNUpWYejuAX7lKkM%0AH1J1%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/1481233475/47fdbad80a17fc4149185618b60a/AD_4nXcnGnEouPD5L_e9RVpEc7qIRW33PSfV4j2vL-Dd4AzoEpm5y5Has1FKjMaAA4_XeTXlJ0EhvvgC6WcbhM-gtFwiybI6xXSO3kA38Tdj_CJhOHkHTu4C_ydluSbIyZLb7Ftc85v6fg?expires=1789486200&signature=34b4eb6b9613c2e40a93e5c77af0fd2f74c5843bfa4fbb134ff9ef2ea11580fe&req=dSQvF8t9noVYXPMW1HO4zcJahpLMzejuvKYKJwypbrOdnNUpWYejuAX7lKkM%0AH1J1%0A)

How do I target specific pages for my survey?
---------------------------------------------

You can target specific pages under **"Choose Where This Survey Shows"** when creating or editing your survey. You'll have two options:

*   **Show on all pages of my site**: your survey will appear across your entire site.
    
*   **Show only on pages that match a rule**: your survey will only appear on the specific page(s) you target. Select your rule type (e.g. "URL ends with") and enter the page URL you want to target. You can add multiple rules if you want to target more than one page.
    

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2548649544/3bed610f1154c258a9d9590b90f2/Choose+Where+this+Survey+Shows.jpg?expires=1789486200&signature=96503ca8b8b0cf82f7e2fe3ad5d686f41f467ac39e2cd95cf27305f2a7382507&req=diUjHs96lIRbXfMW1HO4zZ9Deq3BlqvgfurwhgfxApM6hTklTIkHWR6ydPB4%0ABIlZTjAFZXwUB6zTeEY%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/zmls3dse/2548649544/3bed610f1154c258a9d9590b90f2/Choose+Where+this+Survey+Shows.jpg?expires=1789486200&signature=96503ca8b8b0cf82f7e2fe3ad5d686f41f467ac39e2cd95cf27305f2a7382507&req=diUjHs96lIRbXfMW1HO4zZ9Deq3BlqvgfurwhgfxApM6hTklTIkHWR6ydPB4%0ABIlZTjAFZXwUB6zTeEY%3D%0A)

**How can I customize the appearance of my surveys?**
--------------------------------------------------------

It’s easy! Go to the Survey Design button to personalize your survey with your company’s branding to increase the number of submissions. Customize elements such as:

*   Your brand logo  
    ​
    
*   Background, button, and text colors  
    ​
    
*   Font sizes and styles
    

* * *

**Sharing Surveys with Customers**
==================================

* * *

**What analytics are available for surveys?**
---------------------------------------------

Each survey includes performance data, so you can track engagement and effectiveness.

You’ll be able to see:

*   Total Impressions
    
*   Surveys Started
    
*   Abandoned Surveys
    
*   Completed Surveys
    

* * *

  
**Can I edit a survey after it’s published?**
------------------------------------------------

Yes, surveys can be edited at any time. Just note that **significant changes to questions (like changing types or removing options) may affect how you compare responses** over time.

* * *

  
**How do I duplicate or delete a survey?**
---------------------------------------------

In the **Surveys** section of your dashboard:

*   To **duplicate**, click the **Duplicate** button next to the survey  
    ​
    
*   To **delete**, click the **Delete** button next to the survey you want to remove

**Advanced Features**
=====================

**Do you offer AI-powered insights for Surveys?**
-------------------------------------------------

Yes! HeatmapAI summarization helps you save hours and analyze survey responses at scale. You’ll get automated insights highlighting trends and patterns, so you don’t have to read every response manually.

* * *

**Are surveys mobile-friendly?**
--------------------------------

Absolutely! All surveys are responsive and look great on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices. You don’t need to edit anything in your survey, we did that hard work for you

* * *

  
**Need more help?**
----------------------

Visit our **Help Center** for detailed guides and video tutorials. Look for the “Surveys” section for everything from beginner walkthroughs to advanced tips.

* * *

**How do I contact support if I have questions?**
-------------------------------------------------

If you need further assistance, please contact our support team through your heatmap dashboard or email [support@heatmap.com](mailto:support@heatmap.com)
.

# What are the options for exporting data table information? | Heatmap Help Center

[Skip to main content](https://intercom.help/heatmapcom/en/articles/10024113-what-are-the-options-for-exporting-data-table-information#main-content)

What are the options for exporting data table information?
==========================================================

export data, data table export, CSV format, spreadsheet, custom reports, select columns, filter data, comparison data, date range, download

October 21, 2024

**What are the options for exporting data table information?**

Heatmap.com offers a straightforward and efficient method for exporting your data table information. This feature allows you to analyze your data offline, create custom reports, or share insights with your team. Here's a comprehensive guide to the export option available:

1\. Accessing the Export Feature

To export your data:

\- Navigate to the Data Table view in your heatmap dashboard

\- Look for the "Export" or "Download" button, typically located near the top-right of the data table

2\. Export Format

We currently support one export format:

CSV (Comma-Separated Values):

\- Best for importing into spreadsheet software like Excel or Google Sheets

\- Allows for easy data manipulation and further analysis

\- Compatible with most data analysis tools

3\. Direct Download

When you initiate an export:

\- The CSV file will start downloading immediately to your device

\- No need to wait for emails or access other platforms

4\. Customizing Your Export

Before exporting, you can customize the data included:

a) Select Columns:

\- Choose which specific metrics to include in your export

\- Helps focus on the most relevant data for your analysis

b) Filter Data:

\- Apply any active filters to your export

\- Ensures your exported data matches your current view

c) Date Range:

\- Specify the time period for the data you want to export

5\. Exporting Comparison Data

If you're using the comparison mode:

\- The export will include data for both filters side by side

\- This allows for easy comparison of different segments offline

6\. Data Privacy and Security

\- Exported files may contain sensitive information about your website's performance

\- Ensure you handle these files securely and in compliance with your organization's data policies

7\. Tips for Using Exported Data

\- Regular Exports: Consider scheduling regular exports to track changes over time

\- Combining Data: Use spreadsheet software to combine exports for trend analysis

\- Creating Visualizations: Use the raw data to create custom charts or graphs

\- Sharing Insights: You can easily share the CSV file with team members who need access to the raw data

8\. Troubleshooting

If you encounter issues with exporting:

\- Ensure your browser is up to date

\- Check your browser's download settings

\- Try clearing your browser cache

\- For persistent problems, contact our support team

Exporting your data table information as a CSV file allows you to leverage the insights from your heatmap analysis in various ways. This versatile format provides the flexibility to perform deep analysis, create custom reports, and share valuable insights with your team.

If you have any questions about exporting data or need assistance with using the exported information, please don't hesitate to reach out to our support team.
